title: Show agent status badge in detail view
description: Story 2.19: When agent assigned, show status badge (Running/Idle/Errored) near assignee field. Real-time SSE updates. Click opens agent terminal tab. Show PR link if exists. Runtime duration shown.
design:
## Summary

This task adds an agent status badge to the issue detail view that appears near the assignee field when an agent is assigned to an issue. The badge shows the agent's real-time status (Working/Planning/Ready/Idle/Error/Done), runtime duration, and is clickable to open the agent's terminal tab. It also surfaces a PR link when the agent has created one. The badge updates in real-time by leveraging the existing `useAgentContext()` polling (5s interval) which already provides `getAgentByName()`.

## Technical Approach

### Architecture Decision: Component + Hook

Create a new `AgentStatusBadge` component that sits alongside the `AssigneeDropdown` in the detail view. Rather than introducing new SSE events for agent status (which would require backend changes), we leverage the existing `useAgentContext()` which already polls the loom server every 5 seconds for all agent statuses. This provides effectively real-time updates for the detail view use case.

The badge will reuse the existing `parseLoomStatus()` utility and `getStatusDotColor()`/`getStatusLabel()` helpers from `AgentCard` to ensure visual consistency across the app.

For PR link display, the badge will call `fetchGitStatus()` on mount and periodically (30s) to check if a PR exists for the agent's branch. This is a lightweight GET request and avoids any backend changes.

### Key Design Patterns
- Follow the existing badge pattern established by `BlockedBadge` (pill shape, colored dot, clickable)
- Reuse `parseLoomStatus`, `getStatusDotColor`, `getStatusLabel` from `AgentCard` (already exported)
- Use `useAgentContext().getAgentByName()` for agent status lookup
- Keep the component self-contained with its own CSS module

### Trade-offs
- **Polling vs. SSE for agent status**: The existing 5s poll is sufficient; adding dedicated SSE events would require backend changes for marginal improvement
- **PR link via git status endpoint**: Requires a per-agent API call but avoids adding a new "list PRs" endpoint. We cache the result and poll infrequently (30s)
- **Component placement**: Badge is placed inline next to the AssigneeDropdown in the status row (line ~749-753) rather than in the metadata bar (line ~579-601), because the status row is the editable area and the badge needs to be near the interactive assignee control

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/AgentStatusBadge.tsx`
New component that renders the agent status badge. Props:
- `agentName: string` — the assigned agent's name
- `onOpenTerminal?: (agentName: string) => void` — callback when badge is clicked to open terminal

The component internally:
- Calls `useAgentContext().getAgentByName(agentName)` for real-time status
- Parses status with `parseLoomStatus()`
- Renders a colored status dot + label + duration
- Optionally fetches git status to show PR link
- Is clickable to switch to the Logs tab

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/AgentStatusBadge.module.css`
Styles for the badge:
- Pill-shaped container with border (similar to BlockedBadge)
- Status dot (8px circle, colored by status type)
- Status label text
- Duration text (dimmed)
- PR link icon/button
- Hover and click states
- Cursor pointer when clickable

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.tsx`
**Changes needed:**
- Import `AgentStatusBadge` component
- Import `useAgentContext` hook
- In the `DefaultContent` component, add `useAgentContext().getAgentByName()` lookup
- Place `<AgentStatusBadge>` next to the `<AssigneeDropdown>` in the status row (around line 749-753)
- Only render the badge when `issue.assignee` is set AND `getAgentByName(issue.assignee)` returns a match (i.e., it's an agent, not a human `[H]` assignee)
- Wire the badge click to switch to the "logs" tab via `setActiveTab("logs")`
- Pass any needed callbacks for PR link click

Approximate insertion point (after AssigneeDropdown):
```tsx
<AssigneeDropdown ... />
{agentStatus && (
  <AgentStatusBadge
    agentName={issue.assignee}
    onOpenTerminal={() => setActiveTab("logs")}
  />
)}
```

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.tsx`
**No changes needed** — the helpers `getStatusDotColor`, `getStatusLabel`, and `getAvatarColor` are already exported.

## Dependencies

### Internal Modules
- `useAgentContext` hook (already available via `@/hooks`) — provides `getAgentByName()`
- `parseLoomStatus`, `getStatusDotColor`, `getStatusLabel` from `AgentCard` — for consistent status rendering
- `fetchGitStatus` from `@/api/git` — for PR link detection (checks if agent has pushed and has a PR)
- `LoomAgentStatus`, `ParsedLoomStatus` types from `@/types`

### External Packages
None — no new dependencies required.

### Task Dependencies
- `loomcli-fghge.1` (Full-area IssueDetailView) — **completed** ✓
- `loomcli-fghge.4` (Backend selector dropdown) — **completed** ✓
- The parent epic's terminal infrastructure is already built

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

### Edge Cases
1. **Human assignee (not an agent)**: When assignee has `[H]` prefix or `getAgentByName()` returns undefined, don't show the badge at all
2. **Agent exists but loom server disconnected**: Show badge with "Unknown" status and gray dot; use `useAgentContext().isConnected` to detect
3. **Agent assigned but not yet started**: Status will be "ready" — show gray dot with "Ready" label, no duration
4. **Agent removed while viewing**: Badge disappears reactively when assignee is cleared (existing `AssigneeDropdown` handles the update)
5. **Multiple rapid assignee changes**: Leverage existing optimistic update pattern in `AssigneeDropdown`; badge reacts to prop changes
6. **No PR yet**: Simply don't show the PR link section of the badge
7. **Git status fetch fails**: Silently swallow the error; PR link is optional enhancement, not critical

### Error Handling
- `getAgentByName()` returns undefined gracefully (no agent found = no badge)
- Git status fetch errors are caught and ignored (PR link is best-effort)
- Component handles null/undefined agent status defensively with optional chaining

### Validation
- Agent name must match an entry in the agents list from loom server
- Assignee values with `[H]` prefix are always human, never agents

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (Vitest + React Testing Library)
Create `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/__tests__/AgentStatusBadge.test.tsx`:

1. **Renders badge with correct status**: Mock `useAgentContext` to return an agent with "working" status, verify dot color and "Working" label
2. **Shows duration when available**: Agent with status "working: task-123 (5m)" should show "5m" duration text
3. **Click opens terminal tab**: Click badge, verify `onOpenTerminal` callback fires
4. **Shows PR link when available**: Mock `fetchGitStatus` to indicate a pushed branch, verify PR link renders
5. **Does not render for human assignees**: Pass an assignee with `[H]` prefix, verify no badge
6. **Does not render when agent not found**: `getAgentByName` returns undefined, verify no badge
7. **Handles disconnected loom server**: `isConnected=false`, verify badge shows "Unknown" or graceful fallback
8. **Status updates reactively**: Change the mocked agent status, verify badge updates

### Integration Test
In the existing `IssueDetailPanel.test.tsx`, add a test case:
- Render IssueDetailPanel with an issue whose assignee matches an agent name
- Mock AgentContext to provide that agent's status
- Verify the AgentStatusBadge appears in the status row
- Verify clicking it switches to the "logs" tab

### Manual Verification
1. Open an issue assigned to an active agent in the detail view
2. Verify badge shows correct status dot color, label, and duration
3. Wait 5-10 seconds, verify status updates if agent state changes
4. Click the badge, verify terminal logs tab opens
5. Assign a `[H] human` name, verify badge disappears
6. Unassign the agent, verify badge disappears
7. Check with loom server stopped — badge should show graceful fallback

title: Split view: side-by-side terminal comparison
description: Story 2.20: Split view toggle for two terminal tabs side-by-side. Both panes interactive. Resizable divider. Only available with 2+ tabs. Auto-disable below 900px.
design:
## Summary

Add a split view mode to the TerminalView that displays two terminal tabs side-by-side for comparison. This enables users to view output from different AI backends (e.g., Claude vs Codex) simultaneously, compare terminal sessions, or monitor multiple processes at once. The feature adds a toggle button to the tab bar (only enabled with 2+ tabs), a draggable resize divider between the two panes, and auto-disables below 900px viewport width.

## Conflict Resolution: uffak.21

**This task (fghge.22) is the canonical implementation of split view. uffak.21 should be dropped as a duplicate.**

Both tasks implement identical functionality on the same TerminalView component — creating SplitDivider.tsx, adding split state, adding a toggle button to TerminalTabBar.tsx. They cannot coexist because they modify the same files with overlapping logic. The split view feature serves both epics equally: comparing backends (uffak's stated purpose) and comparing terminal sessions (fghge's stated purpose) are the same UI operation on the same component. There is no meaningful difference in scope or behavior between the two.

Recommendation: Close uffak.21 as duplicate, referencing fghge.22. Any unique requirements from uffak.21's description (e.g., 800px vs 900px threshold — this design uses 900px) can be noted here but do not warrant a separate task.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture**: Extend the existing TerminalView component with split-mode state rather than creating a new wrapper component. The split view is a layout mode change within TerminalView — when enabled, two terminal panes are visible simultaneously instead of one. This keeps all existing tab management, search, clipboard, and connection logic unchanged.

**Key design decisions**:
- The left pane shows the currently active tab; the right pane defaults to the next tab (or first non-active tab) and has its own independent tab selector
- Both panes share the same `instanceRefs` map and tab state — no duplication of terminal instances
- The split ratio is managed via CSS Grid with a draggable divider, stored in component state
- Search operates on the focused pane — focus is tracked via the xterm.js `terminal.textarea` focus event (see Focus Tracking section below)
- The split toggle button sits in the TerminalTabBar alongside the existing full-height toggle

**Trade-offs**:
- Using CSS Grid `grid-template-columns` for the split layout (vs absolute positioning) because it integrates naturally with the flex column layout and handles resize cleanly
- Keeping both terminals always mounted (following the existing pattern where all tab panes are in the DOM) rather than mount/unmount on split toggle — avoids re-creating xterm instances
- Not persisting split state to server (sessionStorage only) since it's a transient UI preference, not session configuration

## Focus Tracking in Split Mode

xterm.js captures focus internally into a hidden `<textarea>` element accessible via `terminal.textarea`. Standard `onFocus` handlers on a container `<div>` will NOT reliably fire because xterm swallows focus into its own textarea/canvas.

**Solution**: Add an `onTerminalFocus` callback prop to `TerminalInstance`. Inside the component, after the terminal is opened and `terminal.textarea` is available, attach a native `focus` event listener:

```typescript
terminal.textarea?.addEventListener('focus', () => onTerminalFocus?.());
```

Clean up the listener on unmount. This fires reliably whenever the user clicks into or tabs into a terminal pane, regardless of how xterm internally manages focus. TerminalView passes a callback that sets `focusedPane` state to `'left'` or `'right'` based on which pane's terminal received focus.

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/SplitDivider.tsx`
A drag handle component for resizing the split panes. Renders a vertical bar between the two panes that can be dragged horizontally. Uses pointer events (`pointerdown` with `setPointerCapture`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`) for cross-browser drag support. Emits ratio changes (0.2–0.8 clamped) to parent. Includes a double-click handler to reset to 50/50. Adds `user-select: none` to document body during drag to prevent text selection. Visually styled as a thin 4px bar with a grab cursor, highlighted on hover/drag.

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/SplitDivider.module.css`
Styles for the split divider: vertical bar with hover highlight, grab cursor, active state styling. Should match the dark terminal theme (#252526 base, #3c3c3c border, accent highlight on hover/drag).

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/SplitPaneSelector.tsx`
A compact dropdown/pill selector for the right pane that lets users pick which tab to display in the secondary pane. Renders as a small bar at the top of the right pane showing the current tab name with a dropdown to switch. Uses the same tab data (id, label, connectionState, brandColor) from the parent. Filters out the tab currently shown in the left pane. Should be visually minimal — a single row with a dropdown arrow, matching the tab bar dark theme. Approximately 28px height.

### 4. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/SplitPaneSelector.module.css`
Styles for the compact pane selector.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalInstance.tsx`
**Changes needed**:
- Add `onTerminalFocus?: () => void` to `TerminalInstanceProps`
- In the main terminal setup effect, after `terminal.open(termRef.current)`, add a `focus` event listener on `terminal.textarea`:
  ```
  const ta = terminal.textarea;
  const focusHandler = () => onTerminalFocus?.();
  ta?.addEventListener('focus', focusHandler);
  ```
- Clean up listener in effect cleanup: `ta?.removeEventListener('focus', focusHandler)`
- No changes to `TerminalInstanceHandle` — focus tracking is fire-and-forget, not imperative

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalView.tsx`
**Changes needed**:
- Add state: `isSplitView` (boolean), `splitRatio` (number, default 0.5), `rightPaneTabId` (string)
- Add `focusedPane` state (`'left' | 'right'`, default `'left'`)
- Add `useEffect` for viewport width monitoring: use `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 900px)')` listener. When viewport drops below 900px, set `isSplitView = false`. This is more efficient than resize event listeners.
- Add `handleToggleSplit` callback that enables split mode and sets `rightPaneTabId` to the first tab that isn't `activeTabId`
- Add `handleSplitRatioChange` callback from the SplitDivider
- Add `handleRightPaneTabChange` callback for the SplitPaneSelector
- Add focus callbacks: `handleLeftPaneFocus = () => setFocusedPane('left')` and `handleRightPaneFocus = () => setFocusedPane('right')` — passed as `onTerminalFocus` to the respective TerminalInstance components
- Modify search handlers to target `focusedPane === 'right' ? rightPaneTabId : activeTabId`
- Modify the `terminalsContainer` rendering: when `isSplitView` is true, use a CSS Grid wrapper with `grid-template-columns: ${splitRatio}fr auto ${1-splitRatio}fr` (left pane, divider, right pane)
- Change terminal pane visibility logic: show a pane if `tab.id === activeTabId` OR `(isSplitView && tab.id === rightPaneTabId)`. For the split pane shown in the right position, wrap it in `.splitPaneRight` with relative positioning instead of absolute.
- When a tab is closed that is currently in the right pane, reset `rightPaneTabId` to another available tab or disable split if only 1 tab remains
- When `activeTabId` changes to the same tab as `rightPaneTabId`, auto-switch `rightPaneTabId` to another tab
- Both visible terminals in split mode need `isActive={true}` so xterm.js fit/render cycles work correctly
- After split toggle and after drag resize, call `requestAnimationFrame(() => { fitAddon.fit() })` on both visible terminals via instanceRefs
- Persist `isSplitView` and `rightPaneTabId` to sessionStorage (alongside existing `terminal-active-tab`)
- Pass `isSplitView`, `canSplit` (tabs.length >= 2), and `onToggleSplit` to TerminalTabBar

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalView.module.css`
**Changes needed**:
- Add `.splitContainer` class: `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto 1fr; height: 100%; min-height: 0;` — the template columns will be overridden inline via style prop for the actual ratio
- Add `.splitPaneLeft` and `.splitPaneRight` classes: `position: relative; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden;`
- Add `.splitPaneRight` with a subtle left border (`border-left: 1px solid #333`) to visually separate panes
- Add `.terminalPaneSplit` variant: uses `position: relative; flex: 1;` instead of `position: absolute; inset: 0;` — needed because split panes use flow layout, not absolute stacking

### 4. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalTabBar.tsx`
**Changes needed**:
- Add props: `isSplitView: boolean`, `canSplit: boolean`, `onToggleSplit: () => void`
- Add a split view toggle button next to the existing full-height toggle button
- Button uses a columns/split icon (Unicode `\u2016` double vertical line or similar visual)
- Button uses the `disabled` attribute (NOT aria-disabled) when `canSplit` is false (fewer than 2 tabs). The `disabled` attribute natively prevents click events and conveys disabled state to assistive technology — `aria-disabled` without `disabled` is an anti-pattern that requires manual event suppression.
- Button shows active state when `isSplitView` is true via `aria-pressed="true"`
- aria-label: "Toggle split view"

### 5. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalTabBar.module.css`
**Changes needed**:
- Add `.actionButton:disabled` style: `opacity: 0.3; cursor: not-allowed;` — uses native `:disabled` pseudo-class
- Add `.actionButton[aria-pressed="true"]` style: `background-color: #3c3c3c; color: #fff;` to indicate active split mode

### 6. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/terminalTabUtils.ts`
**Changes needed**:
- Add constants: `MIN_SPLIT_RATIO = 0.2`, `MAX_SPLIT_RATIO = 0.8`, `DEFAULT_SPLIT_RATIO = 0.5`, `MIN_SPLIT_WIDTH_PX = 900`

## Dependencies

- **External packages**: None — all needed functionality (CSS Grid, pointer events, matchMedia) is native browser API
- **Internal modules**: Depends on existing TerminalView, TerminalTabBar, TerminalInstance, terminalTabUtils, and terminalConnection — no new hooks or API calls needed
- **Task dependencies**: Parent epic `loomcli-fghge` (Detail View with Terminal Tabs) must have the terminal tab infrastructure in place — which it does based on the current codebase

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Tab count drops to 1 while split is active**: Auto-disable split mode, show the remaining tab full-width. Reset `rightPaneTabId` to empty.
2. **Same tab selected in both panes**: If `activeTabId` is changed to match `rightPaneTabId`, auto-switch `rightPaneTabId` to the next available tab. The SplitPaneSelector filters out the left pane's active tab from its options.
3. **Tab closed while shown in right pane**: Pick the first available tab (not the left pane's tab) as the new right pane tab. If only 1 tab remains, disable split.
4. **Viewport shrinks below 900px**: Auto-disable split mode via `matchMedia('(min-width: 900px)')` listener. More efficient than resize events.
5. **Full-height mode + split view**: Both should work together — the full-height overlay (position: fixed) contains the split grid layout inside `.terminalsContainer`.
6. **Split ratio extremes**: Clamp drag ratio to 0.2–0.8 so neither pane becomes unusably small.
7. **xterm fit on split toggle**: Both visible terminals need `fitAddon.fit()` called after split toggle and after drag resize. Use `requestAnimationFrame` delay for layout to settle before fitting.
8. **Search in split mode**: Search operates on the focused pane. Focus tracked via `terminal.textarea` focus event (see Focus Tracking section). The SearchBar UI stays the same — it targets whichever pane's terminal last received focus.
9. **WebGL context**: Two xterm instances with WebGL rendering may compete for GPU resources. The existing fallback to canvas renderer (already in TerminalInstance.tsx) handles this — if one context is lost, it degrades gracefully.
10. **New tab created while in split mode**: The new tab appears in the tab bar normally. It doesn't affect the split layout unless the user switches to it.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
- `SplitDivider`: Test ratio clamping (0.2–0.8), double-click reset to 0.5, pointer event handlers
- `SplitPaneSelector`: Test that it filters out the left pane's tab, renders dropdown with remaining tabs, fires onTabChange

### Integration Tests
- Toggle split mode: verify two terminal panes become visible
- Verify split toggle is disabled with < 2 tabs (uses native `disabled` attribute)
- Close a tab while in split mode: verify graceful fallback
- Resize divider: verify ratio changes and terminals re-fit
- Viewport resize below 900px: verify split auto-disables
- Tab switch in left pane to match right pane: verify right pane auto-switches
- Search in split mode: verify it targets the focused pane

### Manual Verification
1. Open terminal view with 2+ tabs — split button should be enabled
2. Click split toggle — two terminals side-by-side with divider
3. Drag divider left/right — panes resize smoothly, terminals re-fit
4. Double-click divider — resets to 50/50
5. Use right pane selector to switch tabs — right pane shows different terminal
6. Close tab shown in right pane — right pane switches to another tab
7. Close tabs until only 1 remains — split auto-disables
8. Resize browser below 900px — split auto-disables
9. Click into right pane terminal, then Ctrl+F — search operates on right terminal
10. Toggle full-height while in split mode — both panes fill the viewport
11. Refresh page — split state persists via sessionStorage

title: Responsive detail view layout
description: Story 2.21: Below 1024px stack vertically. Below 768px tab bar scrolls horizontally. Touch targets 44px minimum. Split view disabled on small screens.
design:
## Summary

Make the detail view (both IssueDetailPanel and IssueDetailView) fully responsive across tablet and mobile viewports. Below 1024px, the two-column grid layout stacks vertically. Below 768px, the tab bar gains visible horizontal scroll affordances. Touch targets are enforced at 44px minimum throughout. The split view (left content + right sidebar) is disabled on small screens, with the right sidebar content flowing below the main content instead.

This is needed because users access the detail view on tablets and smaller screens where the current fixed-width panel and two-column grid become unusable — text gets clipped, touch targets are too small, and the split layout wastes space.

## Technical Approach

**CSS-only approach using media queries and CSS custom properties.** This follows the established codebase pattern — every existing responsive behavior uses `@media (width <= Xpx)` in CSS Modules. No JavaScript resize hooks needed.

**Key decisions:**
- Standardize on three breakpoints via CSS custom properties in variables.css for this task scope
- Use existing `overflow-x: auto` on tab bar but add scroll fade indicators (CSS gradient pseudo-elements)
- Convert the 2-column CSS Grid (`grid-template-columns: 3fr 2fr`) to single-column (`1fr`) at 1024px
- Add a `--touch-target-min: 44px` design token and apply `min-height`/`min-width` to interactive elements in detail views
- No new React components needed — purely CSS changes with minor JSX class additions

**Trade-offs:**
- CSS-only vs JS hook: CSS is simpler, follows codebase convention, and avoids re-renders. Downside is we can't conditionally render (e.g., hide split view toggle button). But since the task says "disabled on small screens" we can use `display: none` which is sufficient.
- Scroll indicators via CSS gradients vs scroll buttons: CSS gradients are simpler and don't require state management. They fade in/out naturally based on scroll position using `scroll-timeline` or static gradients. Given the codebase has no scroll button pattern, gradients are the lower-risk choice.

## Files to Create

None. All changes are to existing files.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `/internal/webui/frontend/src/styles/variables.css`
**Changes:**
- Add responsive breakpoint custom properties:
  ```css
  --breakpoint-tablet: 1024px;
  --breakpoint-mobile: 768px;
  --breakpoint-small: 520px;
  ```
- Add touch target token:
  ```css
  --touch-target-min: 44px;
  ```
- These tokens document the design system and can be referenced in comments, though media queries require literal values.

### 2. `/internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.module.css`
**Changes:**
- **At 1024px breakpoint**: Convert `.contentGrid` (or equivalent two-column grid container) from `grid-template-columns: 3fr 2fr` to `grid-template-columns: 1fr`. Remove `position: sticky` from right sidebar. Right sidebar content flows below main content naturally.
- **At 768px breakpoint**: Ensure panel takes full viewport width. Tab bar section gets scroll fade indicators via `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements with horizontal gradient overlays. Hide any split-view toggle or resize handle.
- **At 520px breakpoint**: Reduce internal padding from `--panel-padding-md` to `--panel-padding-sm`. Stack header actions vertically.
- **Touch targets**: Add `min-height: var(--touch-target-min)` to tab buttons, action buttons, close button, and any clickable elements in the panel. Apply to `.tab`, `.closeButton`, `.actionButton` (and equivalent classes).

### 3. `/internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailView/IssueDetailView.module.css`
**Changes:**
- **At 1024px breakpoint**: If any two-column layout exists, collapse to single column. Stack metadata bar items vertically.
- **At 768px breakpoint**: Stack header bar actions (Open in Terminal, Copy Link) below title instead of inline. Reduce section padding.
- **At 520px breakpoint**: Further padding reduction. Full-width content.
- **Touch targets**: `min-height: var(--touch-target-min)` on back button, action buttons, metadata items that are clickable.

### 4. `/internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalTabBar.module.css`
**Changes:**
- **At 768px breakpoint**: Add scroll fade indicators to the tab container. Use `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements on the scrollable wrapper with linear gradients (transparent → background-color) on left/right edges, ~20px wide. These indicate scrollable content exists.
- **Touch targets**: Set `min-height: var(--touch-target-min)` on individual tab elements (currently 36px, needs to be 44px). Increase close button hit area to 44×44px using padding (visual size can stay smaller).
- Increase tab padding slightly to accommodate larger touch targets without looking cramped.

### 5. `/internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.tsx`
**Changes:**
- Minor: Add a CSS class (e.g., `styles.tabBarScrollWrapper`) around the tab bar container if one doesn't already exist, to serve as the positioning context for scroll fade pseudo-elements. This is needed because `::before`/`::after` on elements with `overflow: auto` don't scroll with content — the wrapper must be `position: relative` with the pseudo-elements on it.

## Dependencies

- **Internal**: Depends on the existing IssueDetailPanel and IssueDetailView components being stable (they are — recent commits show incremental improvements, not structural changes).
- **External packages**: None needed. Pure CSS changes.
- **Task dependencies**: Parent epic loomcli-fghge should have core detail view structure in place (it does — terminal tabs, inline edit, copy/paste, and comments are already implemented per recent commits).

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Panel at exactly 1024px**: Use `<=` (as codebase convention) so the breakpoint includes 1024px exactly — `@media (width <= 1024px)`.
2. **Tab bar with many tabs**: At 768px, horizontal scroll + fade indicators handle this. The existing `scrollIntoView` call in TerminalTabBar.tsx ensures the active tab stays visible.
3. **Tab bar with only 1-2 tabs**: Scroll indicators should NOT appear if content doesn't overflow. CSS gradient approach with `position: sticky` or checking `scrollWidth > clientWidth` is ideal. Simplest: always show subtle fade indicators — they're harmless when no scroll is needed since content won't be behind them.
4. **Right sidebar content on small screens**: When stacked below main content, it should have a visual separator (border-top or spacing) so it doesn't blend into the main content section.
5. **Touch target increase on tab close button**: The visual icon stays small (current size), but the clickable area expands via padding. Ensure the padding doesn't cause tabs to overlap.
6. **Panel animation on mobile**: The slide-in `translateX` animation should still work at full width. The existing `--panel-width-max: 840px` becomes irrelevant below 520px where the panel is 100% width (already handled).
7. **Keyboard navigation**: Tab bar keyboard nav (`scrollIntoView`) still works with the new scroll indicators since they're purely visual overlays.

## Testing Strategy

### Manual verification:
1. **1024px breakpoint**: Resize browser to 1024px width. Verify the detail panel's two-column layout collapses to single column. Right sidebar content should appear below main content with a visual separator.
2. **768px breakpoint**: At 768px, open a detail panel with 4+ terminal tabs. Tab bar should scroll horizontally with visible fade indicators on the edges. Scroll left/right to verify indicators work.
3. **Touch targets**: Use browser DevTools to inspect interactive elements in the detail view. All buttons, tabs, and clickable items should have at least 44px height (check computed styles).
4. **520px breakpoint**: At 520px, panel should be full width. Header actions should stack. Padding should be reduced.
5. **Split view disabled**: Below 1024px, verify there is no side-by-side layout anywhere in the detail view. Everything should be vertically stacked.
6. **Tab bar with few tabs**: With 1-2 tabs at 768px, verify scroll indicators don't look broken or cover tab content.

### Automated tests:
- No new unit tests needed — these are CSS-only layout changes. Existing component tests (if any) should pass since no logic changes.
- If the project has visual regression testing (e.g., Playwright screenshots), add viewport variants at 1024px, 768px, and 520px for the detail panel and detail view.

### Browser testing:
- Test in Chrome and Firefox (primary targets for CSS `@media (width <= X)` syntax which is supported in both).
- Verify `overflow-x: auto` + pseudo-element scroll indicators render correctly in both browsers.

title: Multi-issue terminal session management
description: Story 2.22: Navigating between issues preserves terminal sessions (tmux alive server-side). Global indicator shows issues with active sessions. Explicit close all sessions option. Handle server restart gracefully.
design:
## Summary

Multi-issue terminal session management enables users to navigate between issues while preserving their terminal sessions. Currently, terminal sessions live in a global TerminalView with no association to issues. This task adds an issue→session mapping layer (Redis-backed), a global indicator showing which issues have active sessions, a \"close all sessions\" action, and graceful recovery when the server restarts. Together these changes make the terminal experience issue-aware: opening an issue auto-connects to its session, switching issues auto-switches terminals, and the user always knows which issues have live sessions.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture**: Extend the existing tabmeta Redis store with an optional \`issue_id\` field on TabMetadata. This avoids a new store and keeps session↔issue mapping in the same Redis hash that already tracks label, notes, and sort_order. A new API endpoint \`GET /api/terminal/sessions/by-issue\` returns a map of issue_id → session names for the indicator system. The frontend gets a new React context (IssueSessionContext) that tracks the issue↔session mapping and is consumed by IssueCard for badge rendering.

**Key design decisions**:
1. **Extend tabmeta, don't create a new store**: The TabMetadata struct already persists per-session data in Redis. Adding \`issue_id\` as an optional field keeps the data model simple and avoids a second scan/lookup.
2. **Naming convention for issue-bound sessions**: Session names use the pattern \`issue-{sanitized_issue_id}\` (e.g., \`issue-loomcli-abc123-5\`). This keeps sessions discoverable via tmux list-sessions and avoids collisions with existing sessions like \`talk-to-lead\`.
3. **Server restart recovery**: The TerminalManager already queries tmux list-sessions on ListActiveSessions(). On startup, the server cross-references live tmux sessions against Redis metadata to rebuild the session map. No new recovery code needed beyond ensuring EnsureDefaults is called with the issue_id field preserved.
4. **SSE for real-time indicator updates**: Broadcast a new \`terminal_session_change\` mutation type when sessions are created/destroyed for an issue. Frontend debounces and refetches the issue→session map.

## Files to Modify

### Backend

1. **\`internal/webui/tabmeta/store.go\`**
   - Add \`IssueID string\` field to \`TabMetadata\` struct (json: \`issue_id\`, omitempty)
   - Update \`Set()\` to persist \`issue_id\` in the Redis hash
   - Update \`parseMetadata()\` to read \`issue_id\` from Redis hash
   - Update \`Patch()\` to support patching \`issue_id\`
   - Add \`ListByIssue(ctx, issueID) ([]TabMetadata, error)\` — scans all metadata and filters by issue_id (acceptable because total session count is low, <50)
   - Add \`ListIssueSessionMap(ctx) (map[string][]string, error)\` — returns issue_id → []session_name for all sessions that have an issue_id set

2. **\`internal/webui/handlers_terminal_sessions.go\`**
   - Add \`handleListSessionsByIssue(tabMetaStore)\` handler: \`GET /api/terminal/sessions/by-issue\` returns \`{issue_id: [session_names]}\` map
   - Add \`handleCloseAllSessions(termManager, tabMetaStore, hub)\` handler: \`POST /api/terminal/sessions/close-all\` kills all tmux sessions, deletes all tab metadata, broadcasts SSE event
   - Extend \`terminalSessionInfo\` struct with optional \`IssueID string\` field

3. **\`internal/webui/handlers_terminal_tabs.go\`**
   - In \`handlePatchTerminalTab\`: accept \`issue_id\` in the PATCH body fields, pass through to tabmeta store
   - When \`issue_id\` is set or cleared on a tab, broadcast SSE event with type \`terminal_session_change\`

4. **\`internal/webui/handlers_terminal.go\`**
   - In \`handleTerminalWS\`: after successful WebSocket attachment, if the session has an \`issue_id\` in metadata, broadcast \`terminal_session_change\` SSE event (so indicators update when a session connects)

5. **\`internal/webui/sse.go\`**
   - Add \`\"terminal_session_change\"\` to the MutationPayload.Type comment for documentation
   - No code changes needed — the existing broadcast mechanism is generic and accepts any type string

6. **\`internal/webui/routes.go\`**
   - Add route: \`GET /api/terminal/sessions/by-issue\` → \`handleListSessionsByIssue\`
   - Add route: \`POST /api/terminal/sessions/close-all\` → \`handleCloseAllSessions\`

7. **\`internal/webui/terminal.go\`**
   - Add \`KillAllSessions()\` method to TerminalManager: iterates all connections, closes PTYs, kills all prefixed tmux sessions. Similar to Shutdown() but does not reset the manager itself.

### Frontend

8. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/api/terminal.ts\`**
   - Add \`listSessionsByIssue(): Promise<Record<string, string[]>>\` — calls \`GET /api/terminal/sessions/by-issue\`
   - Add \`closeAllSessions(): Promise<void>\` — calls \`POST /api/terminal/sessions/close-all\`
   - Extend \`TabMetadata\` interface with optional \`issue_id?: string\`

9. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/useIssueSessionMap.ts\`** (NEW)
   - New hook that fetches and caches the issue_id → session_name[] map
   - Exposes: \`issueSessionMap: Record<string, string[]>\`, \`hasActiveSession(issueId): boolean\`, \`refetch()\`, \`handleMutation(mutation)\`
   - Listens for SSE events of type \`terminal_session_change\` to trigger debounced refetch
   - Used by IssueCard and TerminalView

10. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/useTerminalMetadata.ts\`**
    - Extend to include \`issue_id\` in PATCH calls when linking a session to an issue
    - Add \`linkToIssue(session: string, issueId: string): Promise<void>\` method
    - Add \`unlinkFromIssue(session: string): Promise<void>\` method

11. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.tsx\`**
    - Import \`useIssueSessionMap\` (or receive \`hasActiveSession\` as prop from parent to avoid N+1 hook calls)
    - Render a small terminal icon badge next to the issue ID when \`hasActiveSession(issue.id)\` is true
    - Badge should be a subtle monochrome terminal icon (reuse the NavRail terminal SVG scaled down)

12. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.module.css\`**
    - Add \`.sessionBadge\` styles: small (14×14px) icon positioned inline after the issue ID, with subtle opacity

13. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalView.tsx\`**
    - Accept optional \`issueId?: string\` prop
    - When \`issueId\` is provided and changes: check if a session exists for that issue (via useIssueSessionMap), if yes switch to it, if no create a new tab with session name \`issue-{issueId}\` and link it via PATCH
    - Add \"Close All Sessions\" button in the tab bar area (calls \`closeAllSessions()\` API)

14. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/TerminalView/TerminalTabBar.tsx\`**
    - Add \`onCloseAll?: () => void\` prop
    - Render a \"Close All\" button (trash icon or similar) in the tab bar, enabled only when >0 sessions exist
    - Confirm before executing (window.confirm or small inline confirmation)

15. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/App.tsx\`**
    - Pass \`issueId={selectedIssueId}\` to TerminalView when rendering it
    - When user clicks an issue card that has an active session badge, optionally auto-switch to terminal view (or show a tooltip indicating active session)
    - Provide \`IssueSessionMapProvider\` context wrapper (or just use the hook at App level and pass down)

16. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/api/sse.ts\`**
    - Add \`\"terminal_session_change\"\` to the \`MutationType\` union type

## Files to Create

1. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/useIssueSessionMap.ts\`**
   - React hook for issue→session mapping with SSE-driven refetch
   - ~60 lines, follows the pattern of useTerminalMetadata.ts

## Dependencies

- **Internal**: tabmeta store (Redis), TerminalManager, SSEHub, existing terminal API client
- **External**: No new packages needed
- **Task dependencies**: This task depends on the parent epic (loomcli-fghge: Detail View with Terminal Tabs) being available for integration, but the session management layer can be built independently

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Session name collisions**: If two issues somehow generate the same session name, the second attach will reuse the existing tmux session. The issue_id in metadata determines ownership — last writer wins. Mitigated by including the full issue ID in the session name.
2. **Orphaned sessions**: If the server crashes, tmux sessions persist but Redis metadata may be stale. On startup, EnsureDefaults already reconciles active tmux sessions with stored metadata. Sessions without metadata get defaults; metadata without tmux sessions remains (harmless, shows as disconnected).
3. **Concurrent close-all**: If two clients both trigger close-all simultaneously, KillAllSessions is idempotent — killing an already-dead session is a no-op.
4. **Issue deleted with active session**: Session continues running. The indicator disappears because the issue is gone. User can still access the session from the terminal view's tab bar. No automatic cleanup needed.
5. **Redis unavailable**: All tabmeta operations fail gracefully with error responses. Terminal sessions still work (tmux is the source of truth for session existence), just without metadata/issue linking.
6. **Max sessions reached**: Existing ErrMaxSessionsReached error propagates to frontend. User sees error toast. No special handling needed for issue-bound sessions.
7. **Session name validation**: Issue IDs may contain dots (e.g., \`loomcli-abc.5\`). The session name regex requires \`[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\`. Replace dots with hyphens in the session name: \`issue-loomcli-abc-5\`.

## Testing Strategy

### Backend Tests
- **tabmeta/store_test.go**: Test Set/Get/List with issue_id field, test ListByIssue filtering, test ListIssueSessionMap aggregation
- **handlers_terminal_sessions_test.go**: Test close-all endpoint kills sessions and clears metadata, test by-issue endpoint returns correct map
- **handlers_terminal_tabs_test.go**: Test PATCH with issue_id field, verify SSE broadcast on issue_id change
- **terminal_test.go**: Test KillAllSessions method

### Frontend Tests
- **useIssueSessionMap.test.ts**: Test fetch, refetch on SSE event, hasActiveSession helper
- **IssueCard.test.tsx**: Test session badge renders when hasActiveSession is true, doesn't render when false
- **TerminalView.test.tsx**: Test auto-switch to issue session when issueId prop changes, test close-all button
- **TerminalTabBar.test.tsx**: Test close-all button rendering and click handler

### Manual Verification
1. Open an issue → terminal session created with issue-{id} name
2. Navigate to another issue → previous session preserved, new session created
3. Navigate back → previous session reconnects (tmux alive)
4. Check kanban board → terminal badges visible on issues with active sessions
5. Click \"Close All Sessions\" → all tmux sessions killed, badges disappear
6. Restart server → sessions reconnect, badges reappear
7. Open terminal view directly → existing sessions visible, can switch between issue-bound and global sessions

title: Blocked-by relationship navigation in detail view
description: Story 2.23: Blocked-by section shows clickable chips with status. Click navigates to blocker's detail view. Inline indicator for resolved/in-progress/blocked. Depth limit with view full chain option.
design:
## Summary

Transform the existing DependencySection in the issue detail panel from a flat, non-interactive list into clickable status chips that enable direct navigation to blocker detail views. Currently, dependency items show as plain text rows with ID, title, and remove button. This task converts them into visually distinct chips with inline status indicators (resolved/in-progress/blocked), makes them clickable to navigate to the blocker's detail view, and adds a depth limit with a "View full chain" expand option when there are many blockers.

This feature improves the UX for understanding and navigating blocking relationships, which is critical for project management workflows where blockers need quick investigation.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture Decision:** Use the existing first-level dependency data already returned by `getIssue(id)` via `IssueDetails.dependencies` (typed as `IssueWithDependencyMetadata[]`). No new backend API endpoints are needed — the existing data already includes `status`, `title`, `id`, `priority`, and `dependency_type` for each dependency. The `IssueWithDependencyMetadata` extends `Issue`, so all status information is already available on the client.

**Navigation Pattern:** Thread an `onNavigateToIssue` callback from `App.tsx` → `IssueDetailPanel` → `DefaultContent` → `DependencySection`. When a chip is clicked, it calls `handleIssueClick` in App.tsx, which sets the new `selectedIssueId` and fetches the new issue details. The panel content replaces in-place — this is the existing navigation pattern used by kanban cards and table rows.

**Depth Limit:** Show a configurable number of dependency chips (default: 5) with a "Show all N blockers" / "View full chain" toggle button. This is a simple client-side truncation of the dependencies array, not a recursive tree traversal.

**Key Design Patterns:**
- Chip-style UI follows the pattern used by labels in the detail panel
- Status color-coding uses existing CSS variables (--color-success, --color-warning, --color-danger)
- Click handler reuses the same Issue-based navigation as kanban cards
- Apply same treatment to the "Blocks" (dependents) section for consistency

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/DependencySection.tsx`
**Changes:**
- Add `onNavigateToIssue?: (issue: IssueWithDependencyMetadata) => void` prop to `DependencySectionProps`
- Replace the flat `<li>` dependency items with clickable chip-style elements
- Add inline status indicator (colored dot + status text) to each chip:
  - `closed` → green dot, strikethrough text (already styled)
  - `in_progress` → amber/yellow dot
  - `blocked` → red dot
  - `open` → gray dot (default)
- Make each chip clickable: onClick calls `onNavigateToIssue(dep)` (but only when the callback is provided, to maintain backward compatibility)
- Add `cursor: pointer` and hover state for clickable chips
- Implement depth limit: accept a `depthLimit` prop (default 5). If `dependencies.length > depthLimit`, show only the first `depthLimit` items plus a "Show all (N)" / "Show less" toggle button
- Ensure the remove button still works (stopPropagation to prevent chip click from firing)
- Keep all existing add/remove functionality unchanged

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/DependencySection.module.css`
**Changes:**
- Add `.dependencyChip` styles: inline-flex, gap, padding, border-radius (pill shape), background, hover state, cursor:pointer, transition
- Add `.statusDot` styles: small colored circle (8px) with status-based color classes
- Add `.statusDotClosed` (green), `.statusDotInProgress` (amber), `.statusDotBlocked` (red), `.statusDotOpen` (gray)
- Add `.showMoreButton` styles: text button at the bottom of the list, secondary color, with count badge
- Add `.clickable` modifier class with hover/focus styles
- Adjust `.dependencyItem` to use chip layout instead of row layout

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.tsx`
**Changes:**
- Add `onNavigateToIssue?: (issue: Issue) => void` prop to `IssueDetailPanelProps` and `DefaultContentProps`
- Pass `onNavigateToIssue` down to the `DependencySection` component
- Apply the same clickable-chip treatment to the "Blocks" (dependents) section:
  - Convert `renderDependencyItem` to use the same chip component/pattern
  - Add click handler to navigate to the dependent issue
  - Add status indicators
  - Add depth limit with "Show all" toggle
- Thread the callback through all the right layers

### 4. `internal/webui/frontend/src/App.tsx`
**Changes:**
- Pass `handleIssueClick` (or a wrapper) as `onNavigateToIssue` prop to `IssueDetailPanel`
- The existing `handleIssueClick` callback already handles the navigation flow correctly:
  - Sets `selectedIssueId`
  - Calls `fetchIssue(id)` to load the new issue details
  - The panel content auto-replaces with the new issue
- Since `handleIssueClick` expects an `Issue` object and `IssueWithDependencyMetadata extends Issue`, the types are compatible — no adapter needed

## Files to Create

None — all changes fit within existing files.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed
- No backend changes needed (existing `IssueDetails.dependencies` already provides all required data)
- Depends on parent epic `loomcli-fghge` (Detail View with Terminal Tabs) being in progress, but the DependencySection component already exists and is functional

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Dependency with no status field**: Default to `open` status and gray dot. The `IssueWithDependencyMetadata` extends `Issue` where `status` is optional, so handle `undefined`.
2. **Self-navigation**: If clicking a dependency that is the currently displayed issue, do nothing (the existing `handleIssueClick` in App.tsx already handles this case — returns early if same ID).
3. **Empty dependencies**: Keep existing "No blocking dependencies" empty state. The depth limit toggle should not appear.
4. **Exactly at depth limit**: If `dependencies.length === depthLimit`, show all without the toggle button. Toggle only appears when `> depthLimit`.
5. **Remove button click propagation**: `e.stopPropagation()` on the remove button's onClick to prevent the chip's navigation click from firing.
6. **Rapid clicking between dependencies**: The existing `handleIssueClick` cancels pending panel timeouts, and `useIssueDetail` handles concurrent requests (latest wins), so this is already safe.
7. **Dependency issue has been deleted/tombstoned**: Show the chip but with a muted/unavailable style. The status would be `tombstone` — treat similarly to `closed` but with different visual (crossed out, gray).
8. **Loading state during navigation**: The panel shows its existing loading spinner while fetching the new issue details.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
- **DependencySection.test.tsx**: 
  - Verify clicking a dependency chip calls `onNavigateToIssue` with the correct issue data
  - Verify status dots render with correct CSS classes for each status value (open, in_progress, blocked, closed)
  - Verify depth limit: with 8 dependencies and limit 5, only 5 are shown initially
  - Verify "Show all" button appears when count > limit and clicking it reveals all items
  - Verify "Show less" collapses back to the limit
  - Verify remove button click does NOT trigger navigation (stopPropagation)
  - Verify chip is not clickable when `onNavigateToIssue` is not provided (backward compat)
  - Verify empty state unchanged

### Integration Tests
- **IssueDetailPanel rendering**: Verify the onNavigateToIssue callback is threaded correctly from panel props to DependencySection
- **Dependents section**: Verify the "Blocks" section also renders clickable chips with status indicators

### Manual Verification
1. Open an issue with blocking dependencies in the detail panel
2. Verify each dependency shows as a chip with colored status dot
3. Click a dependency chip → panel should navigate to show that issue's details
4. Click browser back or another issue → verify navigation works correctly
5. Open an issue with >5 dependencies → verify "Show all (N)" button appears
6. Click "Show all" → all dependencies visible, button changes to "Show less"
7. Verify the remove (X) button still works without triggering navigation
8. Verify the "Blocks" (dependents) section has the same chip treatment

title: Owner and assignee management dropdowns
description: Story 2.24: Clickable owner/assignee fields open dropdown. Shows humans and agents grouped by backend. Stop current agent prompt on reassign. Changes reflected on kanban immediately.
design:
## Summary

This task transforms the read-only owner and assignee fields in the IssueDetailPanel metadata bar into interactive dropdowns. The assignee dropdown shows both AI agents (grouped by backend — Claude, Codex, OpenCode) and humans, with real-time availability status. The owner dropdown allows selecting a human owner for attribution. All changes propagate to the kanban board immediately via SSE mutations.

**Why it is needed:** Currently, owner is read-only and assignee can only be edited in the properties section (line 1132). The metadata bar (lines 842-884) shows both fields as plain text. Making these fields interactive in the metadata bar gives users quick access to reassignment without scrolling.

**Addressing prior review feedback:**
- The previous design described `handleBeforeReassign` calling "the loom agent control API" to stop an agent before reassignment, but no such write/control endpoint exists in the codebase. `agents.ts` only has read-only functions (`fetchAgents`, `checkLoomHealth`, `fetchStatus`, `fetchTasks`). The daemon has internal `stopAgent()` but no HTTP endpoint exposes it for individual agents.
- **Resolution: Remove stop-on-reassign from scope.** Reassigning from one agent to another simply updates the assignee field. A confirmation dialog warns the user ("Agent X is currently working on this issue. Reassigning will not stop its current session."). Stopping agents remains the user's responsibility via the terminal session kill button (existing `scheduleSessionKill` in terminal.ts) or daemon CLI. This is the correct separation of concerns — agent lifecycle management is distinct from issue field editing.
- Owner field gap confirmed: `CreateArgs` (protocol.go:105) has `Owner` but `UpdateArgs` (protocol.go:122-174) does not. This task adds it.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture**: Enhance the existing `AssigneeDropdown` (currently at `IssueDetailPanel/AssigneeDropdown.tsx`) to become a grouped, searchable dropdown that merges agent data from the `useAgents()` hook with the existing recent-humans list. Create a new `OwnerDropdown` component following the same pattern but simpler (humans only, no agent integration). Both replace the current read-only metadata spans in the metadata bar.

**Key Design Decisions**:
- **Enhance rather than replace** AssigneeDropdown — it already has optimistic updates, click-outside, escape-to-close, and error rollback patterns. Adding grouped sections for agents extends it naturally.
- **Reuse BackendSelectorDropdown patterns** for agent grouping UI (brand-colored dots, search filtering) but do not use the component directly since it serves a different purpose (single backend selection vs. agent assignment).
- **Owner dropdown is separate** from assignee — owner is always a human (git author email for attribution), while assignee can be human or agent.
- **No stop-on-reassign** — show a confirmation dialog when reassigning from one agent to another, but do not attempt to stop agents. No new backend endpoints needed.
- **SSE "update" mutation** already includes `assignee` field — add `owner` to `MutationPayload` so kanban cards reflect owner changes in real-time.

**Trade-offs**:
- Considered a unified "People Dropdown" for both owner and assignee but rejected: different semantics (owner = human attribution, assignee = who's working including agents). Separate dropdowns are clearer.
- Considered adding a new `POST /api/agents/{name}/stop` endpoint for stop-on-reassign, but that is a separate feature (agent lifecycle management) and should be its own task. Keeping this task focused on field editing.

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/OwnerDropdown.tsx`
New component for editing the owner field. Simpler than AssigneeDropdown — no agent integration, just human names. Features:
- Text input for free-form owner names (emails/names)
- Recent owners list from localStorage (via `useRecentOwners` hook)
- "Remove owner" button to clear the field
- Keyboard support (Escape to close, Enter to submit)
- Optimistic updates with error rollback
- Same visual pattern as AssigneeDropdown with distinct icon (shield/crown for owner vs person for assignee)

Props: `{ owner: string | undefined; onSave: (newOwner: string) => Promise<void>; isSaving?: boolean; disabled?: boolean; className?: string }`

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/OwnerDropdown.module.css`
CSS module for OwnerDropdown. Mirror the structure of `AssigneeDropdown.module.css` with same class names and patterns for consistency.

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/useRecentOwners.ts`
Hook to track recently used owner names in localStorage. Same pattern as `useRecentAssignees` (hooks/useRecentAssignees.ts):
- Storage key: `"beads-recent-owners"`
- Max 5 items
- `addRecentOwner(name)`, `recentOwners`, `clearRecentOwners`
- Case-insensitive deduplication

## Files to Modify

### 4. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/AssigneeDropdown.tsx`
**Major enhancement** — transform from simple text input to grouped dropdown with agents:
- Add `agents` prop: `agents?: LoomAgentStatus[]` — agent list from `useAgents()` hook passed by parent
- Add `agentTasks` prop: `agentTasks?: Record<string, LoomTaskInfo>` — current task per agent for busy status display
- Add search/filter input that filters both agents and recent humans
- Show two grouped sections in the dropdown menu:
  - **"Agents"** section: List agents grouped by backend (using `KNOWN_BACKEND_DEFAULTS` brand colors from `backendDefaults.ts`). Each agent row shows: colored dot (from backend brandColor), agent name, status indicator (idle/working/error from `parseLoomStatus`). Idle agents are clickable; busy agents are greyed out with tooltip showing current task.
  - **"People"** section: Recent human assignees (existing behavior) + text input for new names
- When selecting an agent: save assignee as the agent name (no `[H]` prefix)
- When selecting a human: save with `[H]` prefix (existing behavior preserved)
- When reassigning FROM an agent TO a different assignee: show confirmation dialog warning that the current agent session will not be stopped automatically
- Props remain backward compatible — without `agents` prop, behavior is identical to current implementation

### 5. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/AssigneeDropdown.module.css`
Add styles for:
- `.sectionHeader` — group header label ("Agents", "People") — uppercase, small font, muted color
- `.agentItem` — agent row in the dropdown with hover state
- `.agentStatusDot` — colored status indicator dot (reuse pattern from BackendSelectorDropdown)
- `.agentBusy` — greyed out styling for busy agents with reduced opacity
- `.searchInput` — search/filter input at top of dropdown
- `.backendGroup` — grouped section for agents by backend
- `.confirmOverlay` — confirmation dialog overlay for agent reassignment warning

### 6. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.tsx`
- Import `OwnerDropdown` component
- Import `useAgents` hook (or use existing if already imported for other features)
- Add `useAgents()` call to get agent list and agentTasks
- Add `handleOwnerSave` callback: calls `updateIssue(issue.id, { owner: newOwner })` with optimistic update
- Add `isSavingOwner` state variable
- Replace the read-only owner metadata span (lines 842-861) with `<OwnerDropdown>` component
- Replace the read-only assignee metadata span (lines 862-884) with the enhanced `<AssigneeDropdown>`, passing agents and agentTasks props
- Keep the existing AssigneeDropdown at line 1132-1136 in the properties section — both locations reference the same handler so they stay in sync via shared state

### 7. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/issues.ts`
- Add `owner?: string` to the `UpdateIssueRequest` interface (after `assignee` at line 330)

### 8. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/sse.ts`
- Add `owner?: string` to `MutationPayload` interface (after `assignee` at line 34) so real-time updates include owner changes

### 9. `internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/index.ts`
- Export `useRecentOwners` and its `UseRecentOwnersReturn` type from the new hook file

### 10. `internal/webui/handlers_issues.go`
- Add `Owner *string \x60json:"owner,omitempty"\x60` to `PatchIssueRequest` struct (after `Assignee` field at line 96)

### 11. `internal/webui/handlers_issues_write.go`
- Add `Owner: req.Owner` to the `patchRequestToUpdateArgs` function mapping (after the Assignee mapping, around line 152)

### 12. `internal/rpc/protocol.go`
- Add `Owner *string \x60json:"owner,omitempty"\x60` to `UpdateArgs` struct (after `Assignee` at line 131). The field already exists in `CreateArgs` (line 105) so the daemon already supports storing owner on creation; it just needs to support updating it too.

### 13. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.tsx`
- When `issue.owner` is set, show a small owner indicator (initials badge or small text) in the card footer area near the existing AgentRow (around lines 212-232). This ensures "changes reflected on kanban immediately" per the story requirement.

## Dependencies

**Internal modules**:
- `useAgents` hook (hooks/useAgents.ts) — provides agent list with polling and status
- `useRecentAssignees` hook (hooks/useRecentAssignees.ts) — pattern to follow for `useRecentOwners`
- `KNOWN_BACKEND_DEFAULTS` from `backendDefaults.ts` — brand colors for agent grouping
- `parseLoomStatus` from `@/types/agent.ts` — for categorizing agent availability status
- `updateIssue` API (api/issues.ts) — already supports assignee, needs owner added
- SSE mutation system (api/sse.ts) — already broadcasts updates, needs owner field added

**External packages**: None needed.

**Task dependencies**:
- Parent epic loomcli-fghge (Detail View) must have the base panel — it does (fghge.1 is complete)
- No dependency on agent lifecycle management — stop-on-reassign removed from scope

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Reassigning from agent to agent**: Show confirmation dialog: "Agent X is currently working on this issue. Reassigning will not stop its current session. Continue?" User can proceed or cancel. This is a UI-only confirmation — no backend agent control needed.
2. **Agent becomes busy between dropdown open and click**: Assignment PATCH still succeeds (issue-level operation). The agent's actual availability is reflected on next poll cycle.
3. **Concurrent reassignment**: Last write wins at the API level. SSE mutation updates all connected clients to the final state.
4. **Empty owner field**: Owner is optional. Show "No owner" placeholder in trigger button. "Remove owner" button clears to empty string.
5. **Owner vs assignee confusion**: Distinct icons — shield/crown for owner (attribution), person for assignee (working on it). Tooltip text clarifies semantics.
6. **No agents available (loom server disconnected)**: The "Agents" section in AssigneeDropdown shows "No agents connected" message. The "People" section with manual entry still works. The dropdown degrades gracefully to current behavior.
7. **Backend API unavailable for brand colors**: Fall back to `KNOWN_BACKEND_DEFAULTS` for brand colors (existing pattern from BackendSelectorDropdown).
8. **Long agent/owner names**: Truncate with text-overflow: ellipsis in the trigger button, show full name on hover/tooltip.
9. **SSE reconnection**: Standard reconnect behavior applies. `useAgents` polling provides fallback for agent status even without SSE.
10. **Zero changes scenario**: If owner/assignee update API returns error, optimistic update rolls back and error toast shown (follow existing pattern in handleAssigneeSave lines 642-657).
11. **Assignee dropdown without agents prop**: Backward compatible — renders current behavior (text input + recent humans) when agents prop not provided. This ensures the properties-section AssigneeDropdown (line 1132) can be enhanced independently.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit/Component Tests

**OwnerDropdown.test.tsx**:
- Renders current owner name in trigger button
- Shows "No owner" placeholder when owner is undefined/empty
- Opens dropdown on trigger click
- Text input accepts owner name and submits on Enter
- Recent owners list shown and clickable
- "Remove owner" button clears the owner field
- Closes on Escape key and click-outside
- Optimistic update shows immediately, rolls back on API error
- Disabled state prevents interaction

**AssigneeDropdown.test.tsx** (update existing tests + add new):
- Renders agent list grouped by backend when agents prop provided
- Agents show brand-colored dots and status text
- Idle agents are clickable and trigger onSave with agent name (no [H] prefix)
- Busy agents are greyed out and not clickable
- Search filter narrows both agent and human sections
- "People" section shows recent humans with [H] prefix behavior preserved
- Confirmation dialog shown when reassigning from one agent to another
- Still works without agents prop (graceful fallback to current behavior for backward compat)

**IssueDetailPanel integration**:
- Owner dropdown renders in metadata bar (replacing read-only span)
- Saving owner calls updateIssue with owner field
- Assignee dropdown in metadata bar shows agents from useAgents
- Both metadata bar and properties section AssigneeDropdown stay in sync

### Backend Tests

**handlers_issues_write_test.go**:
- PATCH with `owner` field updates the issue owner
- PATCH with both `owner` and `assignee` updates both fields
- PATCH with empty `owner` string clears the owner

### Manual Verification
1. Open issue detail panel → click owner field → type a name → press Enter → verify owner updates in metadata bar and kanban card
2. Click assignee field → see agents grouped by backend with status dots → select an idle agent → verify assignment updates
3. With an agent assigned → click assignee → select a different agent → verify confirmation dialog appears → confirm → verify assignee changes (old agent session remains running, user can stop it separately)
4. Open two browser tabs → change owner in one → verify the other tab reflects the change via SSE
5. With loom server disconnected → open assignee dropdown → verify "No agents connected" in agents section, manual human entry still works
6. Verify both AssigneeDropdown instances (metadata bar and properties section) stay in sync when either is used
