title: Better Auth Integration: External OAuth & Identity
description: Add centralized authentication to loom via an external Better Auth service. Replaces the existing API key auth entirely. Two modes: open (no auth, local dev) and external (--auth-url pointing to a Better Auth service). Enables GitHub/Google OAuth and user identity flowing through the system. The auth service is a standalone TypeScript app deployable as Docker or self-hosted. Go server validates RS256 JWTs via JWKS. Frontend uses Better Auth client SDK. Organizations and multi-tenancy are out of scope — see follow-up epic loomcli-1voxb.
design:
## Architecture

Two modes only: Open (no auth, local dev default) and External (--auth-url). No API key auth — removed entirely. No organizations/multi-tenancy — that is follow-up epic loomcli-1voxb.

### Algorithm Decision
RS256 everywhere. golang-jwt/jwt/v5 supports it natively (already in go.mod). Better Auth JWT plugin supports it. JWKS uses RSA key type with n/e fields. No EdDSA, no HS256 for user auth.

### Component Diagram

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                  BROWSER                                        │
│                                                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │   Better Auth SDK    │     │            Loom React Frontend               │  │
│  │  (better-auth/react) │     │                                              │  │
│  │                      │     │  AuthGate → SessionProvider → App            │  │
│  │  signIn.social()  ───┼─────┼→ useSession() confirms session                 │  │
│  │  authClient.token() ─┼─────┼→ gets RS256 JWT                     │                         │  │
│  └──────────┬───────────┘     └────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┘  │
│             │                                      │                            │
│             │ OAuth redirects                      │ Authorization: Bearer <jwt> │
│             │ + session mgmt                       │ (every API call)            │
└─────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┘
              │                                      │
              ▼                                      ▼
┌──────────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          │        │                                             │
│   BETTER AUTH SERVICE    │        │          LOOM WEBUI SERVER                  │
│   (Node.js :3000)        │        │          (Go :8080)                         │
│                          │        │                                             │
│  ┌────────────────────┐  │        │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  POST /api/auth/*  │  │        │  │         Middleware Chain              │  │
│  │                     │  │        │  │                                       │  │
│  │  • GitHub OAuth     │  │        │  │  RequestLog                          │  │
│  │  • Google OAuth     │  │        │  │    → RateLimit                       │  │
│  │  • Session mgmt     │  │        │  │      → SecurityHeaders              │  │
│  │  • JWT minting      │  │        │  │        → ExtAuthMiddleware ◄────┐    │  │
│  └────────────────────┘  │        │  │          → CORS                  │    │  │
│                          │        │  │            → Routes               │    │  │
│  ┌────────────────────┐  │  JWKS  │  └──────────────────────────────────┼────┘  │
│  │  GET /api/auth/    │◄─┼────────┼──── JWKS cache (5min TTL)          │       │
│  │    jwks            │  │  fetch  │     verify RS256 sig ──────────────┘       │
│  └────────────────────┘  │        │                                             │
│                          │        │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  ┌────────────────────┐  │        │  │            Routes                    │  │
│  │    Database        │  │        │  │                                       │  │
│  │                    │  │        │  │  GET  /api/config ← public, returns  │  │
│  │  PostgreSQL(cloud) │  │        │  │         {mode, auth_url}              │  │
│  │  or SQLite (self)  │  │        │  │                                       │  │
│  │                    │  │        │  │  GET  /api/issues ← UserIdentity     │  │
│  │  Tables:           │  │        │  │  GET  /api/agents   from context     │  │
│  │  • user            │  │        │  │  GET  /api/events/token ← JWT→opaque │  │
│  │  • session         │  │        │  │  WS   /api/terminal/ws (own auth)    │  │
│  │  • account         │  │        │  │  /api/fleet/* (own auth, exempt)     │  │
│  │  • verification    │  │        │  │                                       │  │
│  │  • jwks            │  │        │  │  /api/loom/* ──proxy──┐               │  │
│  └────────────────────┘  │        │  └───────────────────────┼───────────────┘  │
│                          │        │                          │                  │
└──────────────────────────┘        └──────────────────────────┼──────────────────┘
                                                               │
                                                               ▼
                                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                                    │          LOOM API SERVER (Go :8081)         │
                                    │  /api/agents, /api/tasks, /api/status       │
                                    │  Beads RPC (Unix sock) → Beads Daemon (SQLite)│
                                    │  Redis (optional) — fleet, tabs, history     │
                                    └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Route Exemptions (CRITICAL INVARIANT)

These routes are exempt from ExtAuthMiddleware via isPublicRoute() in auth_routes.go:
- /api/fleet/* — fleet has own auth (X-Fleet-API-Key + HS256 worker JWT)
- /api/internal/workers/* — fleet worker registration (same auth as fleet)
- /api/terminal/ws — terminal has own one-time HMAC token auth
- /api/agents/*/terminal/ws — same
- /health, /api/health — health checks
- /api/config — auth mode discovery (bootstrap, must be pre-auth)
- /api/client-errors — error reporting during auth bootstrap
- /api/csp-report — browser CSP reports
- GET /api/events — SSE handler owns auth via sseAuth middleware
- POST /api/sessions/notify — internal notification endpoint
- All non-/api/ paths — static frontend files

### OAuth Sign-In Flow

```
User clicks "Sign in with GitHub"
    │
    ▼
Frontend: signIn.social({ provider: "github", callbackURL: "/dashboard" })
    │
    ▼
Browser redirects → auth.loomcli.com/api/auth/github
    │
    ▼
Better Auth redirects → github.com/login/oauth/authorize
    │
    ▼
User authorizes → GitHub callback → auth service exchanges code
    │
    ▼
Auth service: creates/updates user, creates session, mints RS256 JWT
    │
    ▼
Redirects to callbackURL → Frontend: useSession() confirms session → authClient.token() gets RS256 JWT
    │
    ▼
AuthContext: setAuthToken(jwt) → fetchApi() sends Bearer <jwt>
    │
    ▼
Go ExtAuthMiddleware: verifies RS256 sig against cached JWKS (no round-trip)
```

### Deployment Modes

```
LOCAL (no auth)                CLOUD (hosted)                 SELF-HOSTED (team)

loom serve                     loom serve \                   loom serve \
                                 --auth-url \                   --auth-url \
                                 https://auth.                  https://auth.
                                 loomcli.com                    mycompany.com
```

### Key Decisions
- No API key auth — removed entirely. Two modes: open and external.
- No organizations/multi-tenancy — follow-up epic loomcli-1voxb
- RS256 signing algorithm (normalized across auth service, JWKS cache, and Go verifier)
- JWT plugin (not stateless sessions) — Better Auth sessions are cookie-based, JWT is sidecar for Go
- 15-min JWT TTL — short-lived, no revocation needed for most cases
- JWKS cache with 5-min TTL + on-demand refresh on unknown kid
- SSE uses opaque token exchange (GET /api/events/token) — JWT never in query params
- Frontend fails CLOSED on /api/config error (shows error page, not open mode)
- isPublicRoute extracted to shared file BEFORE API key removal (prevents terminal/fleet breakage)
- Direct getAuthToken consumers migrated to fetchApi (5 files with raw fetch bypass)
- CLI is local-only today — remote HTTP auth is future work if needed
- Fleet auth, terminal one-time tokens, worker API auth are UNCHANGED
- SSE/terminal connections validated at connect time only (existing behavior)

### Security Model
- RS256 asymmetric verification — no shared secret with auth service
- Algorithm restricted to RS256 exact match (prevents alg:none and confusion attacks)
- jwt.WithExpirationRequired, 5s clock skew leeway
- Token size cap 8192 bytes before parsing
- SSRF protection on JWKS fetcher via safeDialContext
- Empty JWKS response retains cache (prevents lockout)
- Account linking only for trusted providers that verify email
- Auth discovery fails closed — error = error page, not open mode
- OAuth callback validated against trustedOrigins (open redirect protection)

### Out of Scope (Follow-up Epic loomcli-1voxb)
- Organizations plugin and multi-tenancy
- org_id in JWT claims
- Data-layer org isolation (fleet, tabs, issues, session history scoped by org)
- Shared issue boards across team members
- Cross-machine session sync
- Audit logging with userID
- Usage telemetry and billing per org

title: Auth Service: Scaffold and Environment Config
description: Create services/auth/ directory structure. Set up package.json with EXACT version pins (no caret ranges) for security-critical deps: better-auth, hono, @hono/node-server, drizzle-orm, better-sqlite3, pg, zod. Write tsconfig.json. Write src/lib/env.ts with Zod validation: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (min 32 chars AND must be hex or base64 format to ensure randomness — reject low-entropy strings like repeated characters), BETTER_AUTH_URL (valid URL), DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_PROVIDER (pg|sqlite), GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, TRUSTED_ORIGINS (comma-separated), ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS (optional, comma-separated — for registration restriction), ADMIN_USER_IDS (optional), JWT_AUDIENCE (default "loom"), PORT (default 3001). Provide npm script "generate-secret" that outputs openssl rand -hex 32 equivalent. Fail fast at startup on invalid config.
design:
## Summary

Scaffold the standalone Better Auth service at `services/auth/`, establishing the project structure, package manifest with exact version pins (no caret ranges), TypeScript configuration, and fail-fast Zod-validated environment configuration. This is the foundation task — every subsequent auth service task depends on this directory structure and validated env config being in place.

## Technical Approach

**Standalone TypeScript service** at `services/auth/` in the monorepo root. Uses Node.js >= 20 with ESM modules (`"type": "module"`). The env validation module (`src/lib/env.ts`) uses Zod to parse and validate all environment variables at import time, causing an immediate crash with clear error messages on any misconfiguration.

**Key design decisions:**
- **ESM-only** (`"type": "module"` in package.json) — aligns with Hono, better-auth, and modern Node.js conventions
- **`tsx` for dev, `tsc` + `node` for prod** — fast dev loop, clean JS for production Docker images
- **Zod `z.object().parse(process.env)`** — single validation point with typed output. No scattered `process.env.FOO` throughout the codebase
- **EXACT version pins** (no caret/tilde ranges) — security-critical service requires deterministic installs
- **Optional OAuth providers** — GitHub and Google client IDs/secrets are optional so the service can start in minimal mode (local dev with just email/password). Pair constraints enforced via `.superRefine()`
- **`env.ts` exports a frozen typed object** — downstream modules import `{ env }` and get full type safety. No re-parsing.
- **BETTER_AUTH_SECRET entropy validation** — min 32 chars AND must be valid hex or base64 format. Rejects low-entropy strings (repeated chars, dictionary words).
- **DATABASE_PROVIDER explicit declaration** — `pg` or `sqlite`, avoids fragile URL-prefix inference

## Conventions Established

- **Package versioning**: Exact pins only (e.g., `"zod": "3.25.0"`, NOT `"^3.25.0"`) for all dependencies in `services/auth/`
- **Env var naming**: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`, all prefixed naturally (no custom prefix needed since this is a standalone service)
- **Comma-separated list vars**: TRUSTED_ORIGINS, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, ADMIN_USER_IDS — all use the same parse pattern: split on `,`, trim whitespace, filter empty strings
- **Default PORT**: 3001 for auth service (distinct from Go WebUI 8080 and Loom API 8081)
- **Module imports**: Always use `.js` extension in import paths (ESM requirement with NodeNext resolution)
- **Export pattern**: `env.ts` exports `env` (frozen object) and `EnvConfig` (type)

## Files to Create

### `services/auth/package.json`
Package manifest with:
- `name`: `@loom/auth-service`
- `version`: `0.1.0`
- `private`: true
- `type`: `module`
- Scripts:
  - `dev`: `tsx watch src/index.ts`
  - `build`: `tsc`
  - `start`: `node dist/index.js`
  - `typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`
  - `clean`: `rm -rf dist`
  - `generate-secret`: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"`
- Dependencies (ALL exact pins, NO carets):
  - `better-auth`: `1.5.6`
  - `hono`: `4.12.9`
  - `@hono/node-server`: `1.19.11`
  - `drizzle-orm`: `0.45.1`
  - `better-sqlite3`: `12.0.0`
  - `pg`: `8.16.0`
  - `zod`: `3.25.0`
- DevDependencies (exact pins):
  - `typescript`: `5.6.2`
  - `tsx`: `4.20.0`
  - `@types/better-sqlite3`: `7.6.0`
  - `@types/pg`: `8.15.0`
  - `@types/node`: `22.0.0`
- `engines`: `{ "node": ">=20.0.0" }`

### `services/auth/tsconfig.json`
TypeScript config for Node.js server (not browser):
- `target`: `ES2022`
- `module`: `NodeNext` (proper ESM for Node.js — no bundler)
- `moduleResolution`: `NodeNext`
- `outDir`: `./dist`
- `rootDir`: `./src`
- `strict`: true
- `noUnusedLocals`: true, `noUnusedParameters`: true, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`: true, `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames`: true (matching frontend strictness conventions from `internal/webui/frontend/tsconfig.json`)
- `skipLibCheck`: true
- `declaration`: true, `declarationMap`: true, `sourceMap`: true
- `include`: `["src"]`
- `exclude`: `["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.test.ts"]`

### `services/auth/src/lib/env.ts`
Zod-validated environment config. Full schema:

```
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET  — required, min 32 chars, must match hex (/^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/) or base64 (/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/) format. Rejects low-entropy strings like repeated characters.
BETTER_AUTH_URL     — required, valid URL (z.string().url())
DATABASE_URL        — required string (sqlite:./auth.db or postgresql://...)
DATABASE_PROVIDER   — required enum: "pg" | "sqlite"
GITHUB_CLIENT_ID    — optional string
GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET — optional string
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID    — optional string
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET — optional string
TRUSTED_ORIGINS     — optional comma-separated string, parsed to string[], defaults to [origin of BETTER_AUTH_URL]
ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS — optional comma-separated string, parsed to string[] (e.g., "company.com,acme.org"). Empty = no restriction.
ADMIN_USER_IDS      — optional comma-separated string, parsed to string[]
JWT_AUDIENCE        — optional string, defaults to "loom"
PORT                — optional number, defaults to 3001, range 1-65535
NODE_ENV            — optional enum (development | production | test), defaults to "development"
LOG_LEVEL           — optional enum (debug | info | warn | error), defaults to "info"
```

Validation logic:
- Parse `process.env` through Zod schema at module scope (top-level)
- BETTER_AUTH_SECRET validation chain: `z.string().min(32)` then `.refine()` that checks:
  - Must be valid hex (`/^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/`) OR valid base64 (`/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/` with length divisible by 4)
  - Must NOT be all-same-character (e.g., "aaaa...aaa")
  - Error message: "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET must be at least 32 characters of hex or base64. Generate one with: npm run generate-secret"
- `.superRefine()` for OAuth pair constraints: if GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is set, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET must also be set (and vice versa). Same for Google.
- DATABASE_PROVIDER validated as `z.enum(["pg", "sqlite"])`
- Comma-separated list vars (TRUSTED_ORIGINS, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, ADMIN_USER_IDS) use `.transform()`: split on `,`, trim whitespace, filter empty strings
- TRUSTED_ORIGINS defaults to `[new URL(BETTER_AUTH_URL).origin]` when empty/unset
- JWT_AUDIENCE defaults to `"loom"` via `.default("loom")`
- PORT: `z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(65535).default(3001)`
- Export `env` as `Readonly<EnvConfig>` via `Object.freeze()`
- Export `EnvConfig` type for use in other modules
- On validation failure: format all Zod issues (path + message) to stderr, then `process.exit(1)`
- On success: print sanitized startup banner to stdout showing configured providers (GitHub: yes/no, Google: yes/no), database provider, JWT audience, and port. NEVER log secret values.

### `services/auth/src/index.ts`
Minimal entrypoint stub — imports `./lib/env.js` to trigger validation, logs "Auth service starting on port {PORT}" and exits. This file will be expanded by task loomcli-laf73.10 (Hono server). For now it proves the env validation works.

### `services/auth/.env.example`
Template env file showing all variables with placeholder values and inline comments:
```
# Required — generate with: npm run generate-secret
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=
# Required — public URL of this auth service
BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3001
# Required — database connection
DATABASE_PROVIDER=sqlite
DATABASE_URL=sqlite:./auth.db
# OAuth providers (optional — omit for local dev)
# GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=
# GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=
# GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
# GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
# Comma-separated trusted origins (defaults to BETTER_AUTH_URL origin)
# TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8080,http://localhost:5173
# Restrict registration to specific email domains (optional)
# ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=company.com,acme.org
# Bootstrap admin user IDs (optional)
# ADMIN_USER_IDS=
# JWT audience claim (default: loom)
# JWT_AUDIENCE=loom
# Server port (default: 3001)
# PORT=3001
```

### `services/auth/.gitignore`
```
node_modules/
dist/
.env
.env.local
*.db
*.db-wal
```

title: Frontend: App Config Bootstrap and Auth Client
description: Create src/api/appConfig.ts: fetchAppConfig() calls GET /api/config with bare fetch (pre-auth, annotate // allow-raw-fetch). Returns discriminated union type: {mode:'none'} | {mode:'external', auth_url:string}. Use 'mode' not 'auth_mode' (normalized field name). 5-second AbortController timeout. SECURITY: Must fail CLOSED, not open. If /api/config returns error, timeout, non-JSON, or unexpected values, show an error page ('Unable to determine auth configuration — check server connection'). Do NOT default to {mode:'none'} on error — that would silently bypass auth. Only treat mode='none' when the server explicitly responds with it. Module-level cache, never fetched twice. Create src/api/authClient.ts: initExternalAuth(url) creates Better Auth client singleton via createAuthClient({baseURL: url, fetchOptions: {credentials:'include'}}). getAuthClient() returns singleton or throws if not initialized. Add better-auth to package.json dependencies. Add 'better-auth' to manualChunks in vite.config.ts.
design:
## Summary

Create two new frontend modules for auth bootstrapping: `src/api/appConfig.ts` fetches the server's auth mode via GET /api/config (pre-auth, using bare fetch), and `src/api/authClient.ts` initializes a Better Auth client singleton with the `jwtClient()` plugin when external auth is configured. Together, these modules answer "does this server require authentication?" at app startup and, if so, provide the auth client (including `authClient.token()` for JWT acquisition) that downstream components (AuthContext, LoginPage) will use.

This is the client-side counterpart to the Go `/api/config` endpoint (task .18). The app config is the first thing fetched on page load — before any authenticated API calls — and determines the entire auth flow for the session.

## Technical Approach

**Strategy**: Two small, focused modules with clear responsibilities. `appConfig.ts` handles the one-time config fetch with fail-closed security semantics. `authClient.ts` manages the Better Auth client singleton lifecycle, including the `jwtClient()` plugin required for JWT token acquisition. Both use module-level caching (singletons) — config is fetched once, auth client is created once.

**Key design decisions:**

1. **Bare fetch in appConfig.ts (not the API client)**: The config endpoint must be called before auth is initialized — it determines WHETHER auth is needed. Using `fetchApi` would create a circular dependency (fetchApi needs auth token → auth needs config → config needs fetchApi). The `check-no-raw-fetch` linter at `scripts/check-no-raw-fetch.mjs` line 11 excludes `src/api/` via `EXCLUDE_DIRS`, so no annotation or allowlist entry is needed. Do NOT add any `// allow-raw-fetch` or `// pre-auth` comment — the linter simply does not scan this directory.

2. **Discriminated union type for config**: `{mode:'none'} | {mode:'external', auth_url:string}` — using TypeScript's discriminated union pattern makes it impossible to accidentally access `auth_url` when mode is 'none'. The field name is `mode` (not `auth_mode`) per the normalized API contract from task .18.

3. **Fail-closed error handling**: If `/api/config` returns an error, timeout, non-JSON response, or unexpected mode value, the function throws an `AppConfigError`. The caller (App.tsx or a bootstrap component) must catch this and show an error page. We NEVER default to `{mode:'none'}` on error — that would silently bypass authentication, which is a security vulnerability.

4. **AbortController timeout (5 seconds)**: Config discovery is a quick probe. If the server doesn't respond in 5 seconds, something is wrong. We fail fast rather than leaving the user staring at a blank screen.

5. **Module-level promise cache**: `fetchAppConfig()` stores the in-flight promise in a module-level variable and returns the cached result on subsequent calls. This pattern matches `editors.ts`, `workspace.ts`, and `backends.ts`. The promise itself is cached (not just the result) so concurrent calls during initialization are deduplicated.

6. **jwtClient() plugin in authClient.ts (CRITICAL)**: The Better Auth client must include `jwtClient()` from `better-auth/client/plugins` in its `plugins` array. Without this plugin, `authClient.token()` does not exist, and the entire JWT acquisition flow (session cookie → RS256 JWT) breaks. The server-side JWT plugin (task .4) exposes `POST /api/auth/token`; the client-side `jwtClient()` plugin provides the `token()` method that calls this endpoint. The `token()` method returns an RS256-signed JWT that the Go server validates.

7. **Import from `better-auth/react`**: Use `createAuthClient` from `better-auth/react` (not `better-auth/client`) so the returned client includes React hooks like `useSession()`. This is what task .16 (AuthContext) needs. The client is created lazily via `initExternalAuth(url)` and accessed via `getAuthClient()`.

8. **Separate manualChunk for better-auth**: Add `'better-auth'` to `manualChunks` in `vite.config.ts` so it does not bloat the main bundle. Better Auth is only loaded when mode is 'external'.

## Conventions Established

- **`jwtClient()` plugin is required**: Any `createAuthClient` call in this codebase MUST include `jwtClient()` in the plugins array. Without it, `.token()` is unavailable and JWT acquisition fails.
- **Import paths**: Server-side plugin: `import { jwt } from "better-auth/plugins"`. Client-side plugin: `import { jwtClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins"`. Client creation: `import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react"`.
- **No linter annotations in src/api/**: The `check-no-raw-fetch` linter excludes `src/api/` entirely (EXCLUDE_DIRS at line 11). Do not add `// allow-raw-fetch` or similar annotations — they are unnecessary noise.
- **JWKS path**: Better Auth serves JWKS at `/api/auth/jwks` (not `/.well-known/jwks.json`). This is the default path used by the JWT plugin (task .4).
- **Module-level promise cache pattern**: Cache the promise (not just the result) to deduplicate concurrent calls, following `editors.ts`, `workspace.ts`, `backends.ts`.

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/appConfig.ts`

New module. Exports:

```typescript
// Type definitions
export type AppConfig =
  | { mode: 'none' }
  | { mode: 'external'; auth_url: string };

export class AppConfigError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, public cause?: unknown) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'AppConfigError';
  }
}

// Module-level cache (promise-based to dedup concurrent calls)
let configPromise: Promise<AppConfig> | null = null;

export async function fetchAppConfig(): Promise<AppConfig> {
  if (configPromise) return configPromise;
  configPromise = doFetch();
  return configPromise;
}
```

Internal `doFetch()` implementation:
- Creates AbortController with 5-second timeout via `setTimeout`
- Calls `fetch('/api/config', { headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } })` — bare fetch, no annotations needed
- Wraps entire fetch logic in try/catch/finally; the `finally` block calls `clearTimeout` to prevent timer leaks
- On non-ok response: throws `AppConfigError('Server returned <status>')`
- Checks `Content-Type` header includes `application/json` before parsing — if `text/html` (SPA catch-all fallback), throws `AppConfigError('Server returned non-JSON response')`
- Parses JSON via `response.json()`
- Validates response shape: must have `mode` field that is either `'none'` or `'external'`
- When mode is `'external'`, validates `auth_url` is a non-empty string
- When mode is `'none'`, returns `{ mode: 'none' }` (strips any unexpected fields)
- On any validation failure: throws `AppConfigError` with descriptive message
- On timeout (AbortError where timeout flag is set): throws `AppConfigError('Config request timed out')`
- On network error (other catch): throws `AppConfigError('Unable to reach server', cause)`
- **On rejection, resets `configPromise` to `null`** so retry is possible on refresh. Pattern: `configPromise = doFetch().catch(err => { configPromise = null; throw err; });`

Error messages are user-friendly since they are shown on error pages downstream. The generic display message is: "Unable to determine auth configuration — check server connection".

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/authClient.ts`

New module. Exports:

```typescript
import { createAuthClient } from 'better-auth/react';
import { jwtClient } from 'better-auth/client/plugins';

type AuthClient = ReturnType<typeof createAuthClient<{
  plugins: [ReturnType<typeof jwtClient>];
}>>;

let client: AuthClient | null = null;

export function initExternalAuth(authUrl: string): AuthClient {
  if (client) return client;
  client = createAuthClient({
    baseURL: authUrl,
    fetchOptions: {
      credentials: 'include',
    },
    plugins: [
      jwtClient(),
    ],
  });
  return client;
}

export function getAuthClient(): AuthClient {
  if (!client) {
    throw new Error(
      'Auth client not initialized. Call initExternalAuth() first.'
    );
  }
  return client;
}
```

Design notes:
- `jwtClient()` is CRITICAL — it adds the `token()` method to the client. Without it, `getAuthClient().token()` does not exist and JWT acquisition fails entirely. The server-side counterpart is the `jwt()` plugin in `services/auth/src/auth.ts` (task .4).
- `initExternalAuth` is idempotent — calling it twice with the same URL returns the same singleton.
- `getAuthClient` throws if called before initialization — this is a programming error, not a user-facing condition.
- The `credentials: 'include'` option ensures cookies are sent cross-origin for the OAuth flow and token exchange.
- The type parameter `<{ plugins: [ReturnType<typeof jwtClient>] }>` ensures TypeScript infers the `token()` method on the client. Without this generic parameter, the client type would not include the JWT plugin methods.
- `token()` calls `POST /api/auth/token` on the auth service (at the `baseURL`), exchanging the session cookie for an RS256 JWT. The returned JWT is what gets sent as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` to the Go server.

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/__tests__/appConfig.test.ts`

New test file. Uses vitest with jsdom environment (directive: `@vitest-environment jsdom`). Follow the `editors.test.ts` pattern: use `vi.resetModules()` + dynamic import in `beforeEach` to get fresh module instances with empty caches.

Mock `global.fetch` directly (same pattern as `client.test.ts`).

Test cases:
- `fetchAppConfig returns {mode:'none'} for none response` — mock fetch returning `{mode:"none"}` with JSON content-type, verify return value
- `fetchAppConfig returns {mode:'external', auth_url} for external response` — mock fetch returning `{mode:"external",auth_url:"https://auth.example.com"}`, verify return value
- `fetchAppConfig caches result on success (fetch called once)` — call twice, assert fetch called once
- `fetchAppConfig resets cache on failure (allows retry)` — first call errors, second call fetches again
- `fetchAppConfig deduplicates concurrent calls` — start two calls simultaneously, assert fetch called once
- `fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on network error` — mock fetch rejection
- `fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on timeout` — mock fetch that never resolves + verify timeout fires
- `fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on non-JSON response` — mock 200 with text/html Content-Type
- `fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on HTTP error status` — mock 500 response
- `fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on unknown mode value` — mock `{mode:"magic"}`
- `fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError when external mode missing auth_url` — mock `{mode:"external"}` with no auth_url
- `fetchAppConfig strips unexpected fields from none response` — mock `{mode:"none",extra:"field"}`, verify return is just `{mode:"none"}`

### 4. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/__tests__/authClient.test.ts`

New test file. Uses vitest with jsdom environment. Mocks `better-auth/react` and `better-auth/client/plugins` modules.

Test cases:
- `initExternalAuth creates client with correct baseURL, credentials, and jwtClient plugin` — verify `createAuthClient` called with expected args including plugins array containing jwtClient result
- `initExternalAuth returns same singleton on repeated calls` — call twice, verify `createAuthClient` called once
- `getAuthClient returns initialized client` — init first, then get
- `getAuthClient throws when not initialized` — call without init, verify error thrown

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/package.json`

Add `better-auth` to dependencies:

```json
"dependencies": {
  ...existing...,
  "better-auth": "^1.5.6",
  ...
}
```

Place alphabetically among existing dependencies (after `@xyflow/react`, before `codemirror-lang-diff`).

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/vite.config.ts`

Add `better-auth` to `manualChunks` in rollup output options:

```typescript
manualChunks: {
  react: ["react", "react-dom"],
  "react-flow": ["@xyflow/react"],
  "better-auth": ["better-auth"],
  codemirror: [...existing...],
},
```

Place alphabetically or logically among existing chunks.

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/index.ts`

Add re-exports for the new modules at the end of the file:

```typescript
// App config API (auth mode discovery)
export { fetchAppConfig, AppConfigError } from "./appConfig";
export type { AppConfig } from "./appConfig";

// Auth client (Better Auth integration)
export { initExternalAuth, getAuthClient } from "./authClient";
```

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. The existing `src/api/config.ts` handles backend AI config (`/api/config/backend`), which is entirely unrelated to auth config discovery (`/api/config`). No other files in `src/api/` use bare fetch or have auth bootstrapping patterns. The `better-auth/client/plugins` import is new to the frontend — no existing files reference it.

## Dependencies

### External packages
- `better-auth` (^1.5.6) — provides `createAuthClient` from `better-auth/react` and `jwtClient` from `better-auth/client/plugins`. Single package includes server, client, plugins, and React hooks.

### Internal modules
- None — both new files are leaf modules with no internal API client dependencies (appConfig uses bare fetch, authClient uses better-auth directly).

### Task dependencies
- **loomcli-laf73.18** (Go: /api/config endpoint) — MUST be implemented first for manual verification. Without the backend endpoint, `fetchAppConfig()` will get a 404 or SPA fallback HTML. The tests mock fetch so they can be written independently.
- **loomcli-laf73.4** (Auth Service: JWT Plugin) — Already closed. Confirms the server-side JWT plugin exposes `POST /api/auth/token` and `GET /api/auth/jwks`. The `jwtClient()` client plugin calls `POST /api/auth/token` to exchange session cookies for JWTs.

### What this blocks
- **loomcli-laf73.16** (Frontend: AuthContext) — consumes `getAuthClient()` to call `.token()` for JWT acquisition and `useSession()` for session tracking.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **SPA catch-all returning HTML for /api/config**: If the Go endpoint is not registered yet (dependency .18 not landed), the request hits the SPA catch-all and returns HTML with status 200. `fetchAppConfig()` checks `Content-Type` for `application/json` — if it is `text/html`, throw `AppConfigError('Server returned non-JSON response')`. This prevents silently treating the SPA HTML as config.

2. **Unexpected mode values**: If the server returns `mode: "password"` or some future mode the frontend does not understand, `fetchAppConfig()` throws `AppConfigError('Unknown auth mode: password')`. This is fail-closed — we do not guess what to do with unknown modes.

3. **Missing auth_url in external mode**: If `mode: "external"` but `auth_url` is missing, empty, or not a string, throw `AppConfigError('External auth mode missing auth_url')`. This prevents initializing Better Auth with a bad URL.

4. **Network error vs timeout**: Both throw `AppConfigError` but with different messages. Network error: "Unable to reach server". Timeout: "Config request timed out". These are user-facing messages shown on the error page. Distinguish via an internal `timedOut` flag set before aborting (same pattern as `client.ts` line 100-105).

5. **Cache reset on failure**: If `doFetch()` rejects, the `.catch` handler resets `configPromise` to `null` before re-throwing. This allows the user to retry (e.g., after fixing their network connection) without needing a full page reload. On success, the cache is permanent for the page lifecycle.

6. **Concurrent initialization**: Multiple components calling `fetchAppConfig()` simultaneously all receive the same promise. No duplicate network requests. Same pattern as `editors.ts` (line 30-31).

7. **better-auth import when mode is 'none'**: `authClient.ts` is only imported when mode is `'external'`. Combined with the `manualChunks` config, this means the better-auth bundle is never loaded when auth is disabled. Tree-shaking and code splitting handle this automatically — the caller (task .16's AuthContext) conditionally imports `authClient.ts`.

8. **AbortController cleanup**: The timeout's `clearTimeout` is called in a `finally` block to prevent timer leaks, even on error paths. Pattern matches `client.ts` lines 102-107.

9. **jwtClient() not included (programming error)**: If someone creates a new `createAuthClient` call without `jwtClient()`, the `.token()` method will not exist. This is caught at compile time by TypeScript (the type will not have a `token` property). The Conventions Established section documents this requirement.

10. **Auth service URL format**: `initExternalAuth` passes the URL directly to `createAuthClient({baseURL})`. Better Auth handles URL normalization. The URL comes from the `/api/config` response, which in turn comes from the Go server's `--auth-url` flag (validated by task .13).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fetchAppConfig()` returns `{mode:'none'}` when the server responds with `{"mode":"none"}` and status 200.
2. `fetchAppConfig()` returns `{mode:'external', auth_url:'https://...'} ` when the server responds with `{"mode":"external","auth_url":"https://..."}` and status 200.
3. `fetchAppConfig()` throws `AppConfigError` (NOT returns `{mode:'none'}`) when the server returns a non-200 status, non-JSON body, network error, timeout, or unexpected mode value.
4. `fetchAppConfig()` calls `fetch` at most once regardless of how many concurrent callers invoke it.
5. After a failed `fetchAppConfig()`, the next call retries (does not return the cached rejection).
6. `initExternalAuth(url)` creates a Better Auth client with `jwtClient()` in its plugins array.
7. `getAuthClient().token` is a function (the jwtClient plugin exposes it) — NOT undefined.
8. `getAuthClient()` throws if called before `initExternalAuth()`.
9. `better-auth` appears in `package.json` dependencies.
10. `better-auth` has its own `manualChunks` entry in `vite.config.ts`.
11. `npm run typecheck` passes with zero errors.
12. `npm run lint` passes.
13. `npm run check:arch` passes (specifically `check:no-raw-fetch` must not flag appConfig.ts).
14. All new tests pass via `npm run test:unit`.
15. The `src/api/index.ts` barrel re-exports `fetchAppConfig`, `AppConfigError`, `AppConfig`, `initExternalAuth`, and `getAuthClient`.

## Testing Strategy

### Automated Tests

Run after implementation:
```bash
cd internal/webui/frontend
npm install                    # Install better-auth
npm run test:unit              # Run vitest
npm run typecheck              # TypeScript compilation
npm run lint                   # ESLint
npm run check:arch             # Architecture checks (no-raw-fetch, etc.)
```

### Unit Tests (appConfig.test.ts)

Use `@vitest-environment jsdom` directive. Follow the `editors.test.ts` pattern for module cache isolation: `vi.resetModules()` + dynamic import in `beforeEach`. Mock `global.fetch` directly (same pattern as `client.test.ts`).

Each test should:
1. Reset the module via `vi.resetModules()` and re-import `appConfig` to get a fresh cache
2. Mock fetch to return specific responses (including Content-Type header)
3. Assert the returned config shape or thrown error type and message

For timeout tests, use `vi.useFakeTimers()` to advance time without waiting.

### Unit Tests (authClient.test.ts)

Use `@vitest-environment jsdom` directive. Mock both `better-auth/react` and `better-auth/client/plugins` modules via `vi.mock()`. The mock for `createAuthClient` should return a mock object with a `token` function (confirming jwtClient integration). The mock for `jwtClient` should return a sentinel object that can be verified in the plugins array.

Use `vi.resetModules()` + dynamic import in `beforeEach` to reset the singleton between tests.

### Manual Verification (requires task .18)

1. `loom serve` → `curl localhost:8080/api/config` → verify JSON response
2. Open browser → check DevTools Network tab → `/api/config` called once on load
3. Verify no `better-auth` chunk loaded when mode is `none` (check Network tab for chunk requests)
4. With `--auth-url` flag → verify config returns external mode and better-auth chunk loads

title: Frontend: Remove API Key Auth System
description: Remove the entire API key auth path from the frontend. In client.ts: remove the /api/auth/token fetch logic from initAuth(), remove the apikey-specific code paths. Remove authState 'disabled' (was for --no-auth detection via 404 on /api/auth/token). Simplify AuthState to: 'initializing' | 'authenticated' | 'failed'. Export setAuthToken() and setAuthState() for AuthContext to use. The 401 retry interceptor in fetchApi must NOT try to re-fetch /api/auth/token — in external mode it should trigger a session re-check instead. NOTE: Direct getAuthToken() consumers (agents.ts, observability.ts, usage.ts, logs.ts, sessions.ts) are migrated to fetchApi in separate ticket .28.
design:
## Summary

Remove the entire API key authentication path from the frontend client module (client.ts). Currently, the frontend bootstraps auth by fetching a pre-shared API key from GET /api/auth/token — the "apikey" auth mode. This task strips all that logic and simplifies the auth state machine to three states: 'none' (no auth), 'authenticated' (has a valid JWT), and 'failed' (auth attempted but failed). After this change, client.ts becomes a passive token holder — it never fetches tokens itself. Instead, the AuthContext (task .16) calls the exported setAuthToken()/setAuthState() functions to inject the JWT.

## Technical Approach

### Key Design Decision: client.ts Becomes a Dumb Token Store

client.ts will no longer have any auth-fetching logic. The complexity of auth initialization moves to the AuthContext (.16) and boot sequence (.21). client.ts only needs to:
1. Hold a token in memory
2. Inject it as a Bearer header on API calls
3. Expose setters for external callers to manage auth state
4. Dispatch a CustomEvent on 401 so React can respond

### AuthState Type Change

The AuthState type changes from four states to three:

**Remove:** 'initializing', 'disabled'
**Keep:** 'authenticated', 'failed'
**Add:** 'none'

Final type: `'none' | 'authenticated' | 'failed'`

| State | Meaning | Default? |
|-------|---------|----------|
| 'none' | No auth token set (startup default, or no-auth mode, or after sign-out) | Yes (initial) |
| 'authenticated' | Has a valid JWT token (set externally via setAuthToken) | |
| 'failed' | Auth was attempted but failed (kept for SSE reconnection compat in sse.ts) | |

The default changes from 'initializing' to 'none'. This is safe because:
- In no-auth mode, 'none' is the correct permanent state
- In external auth mode, AuthContext (.16) will call setAuthToken() → transitions to 'authenticated'
- sse.ts checks `getAuthState() === 'failed'` before attempting reconnection with re-auth — this still works

### 401 Handler: Event Dispatch Approach

On receiving a 401 response, the fetchApi 401 handler will:
1. Clear the current authToken (set to null)
2. Dispatch `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('auth-token-expired'))` so AuthContext (.16) can trigger a session refresh via Better Auth
3. Throw an ApiError(401, ...) — the request is NOT retried

This approach is chosen over "just throw" because:
- Task .16 (AuthContext) design explicitly listens for `CustomEvent('auth-token-expired')` to trigger debounced session refresh via `getSession()`
- Without the event, AuthContext would have no signal that a token refresh is needed
- The retry logic is removed entirely — after the session refresh, subsequent requests will naturally use the new token

The 401 handler fires only when `authToken !== null` (same guard as today), preventing infinite dispatch when there's no token.

### setAuthToken() Semantics

The new exported `setAuthToken(token)` function:
- Sets the module-level `authToken` variable
- When token is non-null: also calls `setAuthState('authenticated')`
- When token is null: also calls `setAuthState('none')`

This provides a single call site for AuthContext to manage both token and state atomically.

### setAuthState() Export

The existing private `setAuthState` function is exported as-is. This allows AuthContext to set 'failed' state directly (e.g., on auth service errors) without going through setAuthToken.

## Conventions Established

- **AuthState values**: 'none' | 'authenticated' | 'failed' — all sibling tasks must use these exact values
- **401 signal mechanism**: `CustomEvent('auth-token-expired')` dispatched on window — AuthContext (.16) listens for this
- **Token management pattern**: External callers use setAuthToken(token) / setAuthToken(null) — never set authToken directly
- **No auth-fetching in client.ts**: All token acquisition happens in AuthContext or boot sequence, never in the API client layer

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/client.ts`

**Remove entirely:**
- The `initAuth()` function (lines 116-197) — no more /api/auth/token fetching
- The `pendingAuthPromise` variable (line 49) — only used by initAuth deduplication
- The `isTransientFailure()` helper (lines 100-107) — only used by initAuth retry logic
- The `_retried` parameter from `fetchApi` signature (line 211) — only used by 401 retry

**Change AuthState type (lines 36-40):**
- From: `'initializing' | 'authenticated' | 'disabled' | 'failed'`
- To: `'none' | 'authenticated' | 'failed'`

**Change default auth state (line 41):**
- From: `let authState: AuthState = 'initializing';`
- To: `let authState: AuthState = 'none';`

**Export setAuthState (line 68):**
- Change `function setAuthState(state: AuthState): void` to `export function setAuthState(state: AuthState): void`

**Add setAuthToken export (after getAuthToken, around line 204):**
```typescript
export function setAuthToken(token: string | null): void {
  authToken = token;
  setAuthState(token !== null ? 'authenticated' : 'none');
}
```

**Replace 401 interceptor block (lines 260-267):**
- From: the existing block that calls `initAuth({ maxRetries: 0 })` and retries the request
- To:
```typescript
if (response.status === 401 && authToken !== null) {
  authToken = null;
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('auth-token-expired'));
  }
}
```
This fires the event and then falls through to the existing error handling below (parses error body, throws ApiError).

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/index.ts`

**Remove from exports (line 8):**
- `initAuth` — no longer exists

**Add to exports:**
- `setAuthToken` — new export from client.ts
- `setAuthState` — newly exported from client.ts

The exports block becomes:
```typescript
export {
  ApiError,
  get,
  post,
  put,
  patch,
  del,
  setAuthToken,
  setAuthState,
  getAuthToken,
  getAuthState,
  onAuthStateChange,
} from "./client";
```

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/src/main.tsx`

**Remove:**
- The `initAuth, getAuthState` import from `@/api` (line 6)
- The entire `initAuth().then().catch().finally()` chain (lines 67-101)

**Replace with direct render:**
```typescript
createRoot(rootElement).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <ErrorBoundary
      onError={(error, errorInfo) => {
        reportError("react-error", error, {
          componentStack: errorInfo.componentStack ?? undefined,
        });
      }}
    >
      <ToastProvider>
        <WorkspaceProvider>
          <AgentProvider>
            <IssueSessionWrapper>{getComponent()}</IssueSessionWrapper>
          </AgentProvider>
        </WorkspaceProvider>
      </ToastProvider>
    </ErrorBoundary>
  </StrictMode>,
);
```

Note: The full boot sequence rewiring (fetchAppConfig → conditional auth → provider tree) is task .21. This task only removes the initAuth dependency so the app renders immediately without waiting for token acquisition.

### 4. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/sse.ts`

**Remove from imports (line 10):**
- `initAuth` — no longer exists

**Remove re-auth block in connect() (lines 122-126):**
```typescript
// Remove this entire block:
if (getAuthToken() === null && getAuthState() === "failed") {
  await initAuth({ maxRetries: 0 }).catch(() => {});
}
```

**Keep unchanged:**
- `getAuthToken` import — still needed for SSE URL construction
- `getAuthState` import — still needed (sse.ts may still check state for reconnection logic)
- The full SSE token exchange rewrite is task .23; this task only removes the initAuth dependency

### 5. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/client.test.ts`

**Rewrite the Auth describe block.** Remove all initAuth-related tests and replace with tests for the new API surface.

**Remove tests:**
- `initAuth retries on 500`
- `initAuth does NOT retry on 403`
- `initAuth does NOT retry on 404`
- `initAuth sets state to authenticated on success`
- `initAuth sets state to disabled when 200 response has text/html Content-Type`
- `initAuth sets state to disabled when 200 response has no Content-Type header`
- `initAuth sets state to failed after all retries exhausted`
- `fetchApi 401 interceptor - re-auth succeeds`
- `fetchApi 401 interceptor - re-auth fails`
- `fetchApi 401 does not retry infinitely`
- `concurrent initAuth calls are deduplicated`
- `initAuth with maxRetries=0 does not retry on network error`
- The `resetAuthState()` helper that calls initAuth

**Remove from imports:**
- `initAuth` — no longer exists

**Add to imports:**
- `setAuthToken`, `setAuthState` from './client'

**Add new tests:**

1. `setAuthToken(token) sets token and transitions to 'authenticated'` — call setAuthToken('jwt-123'), verify getAuthToken() returns 'jwt-123' and getAuthState() returns 'authenticated'

2. `setAuthToken(null) clears token and transitions to 'none'` — call setAuthToken(null), verify getAuthToken() returns null and getAuthState() returns 'none'

3. `setAuthState('failed') transitions state correctly` — call setAuthState('failed'), verify getAuthState() returns 'failed'

4. `default auth state is 'none'` — on fresh module load, getAuthState() returns 'none'. Note: since vitest re-uses module cache, this test must account for state from prior tests. Use setAuthToken(null) to reset to 'none' first if needed, or rely on test ordering carefully.

5. `onAuthStateChange fires when setAuthToken is called` — register listener, call setAuthToken('test'), verify callback received 'authenticated'

6. `fetchApi injects Bearer header when token is set via setAuthToken` — call setAuthToken('my-jwt'), then call get(), verify Authorization header is 'Bearer my-jwt'

7. `fetchApi does NOT inject header when token is null` — call setAuthToken(null), then call get(), verify no Authorization header

8. `explicit Authorization header is not overridden by setAuthToken` — call setAuthToken('default'), then call get() with explicit Authorization header, verify the explicit header wins

9. `401 response dispatches auth-token-expired event` — call setAuthToken('my-jwt'), mock fetch to return 401, add event listener for 'auth-token-expired', call get(), verify event was dispatched and request throws ApiError(401)

10. `401 response does NOT dispatch event when token is null` — call setAuthToken(null), mock 401, verify no 'auth-token-expired' event dispatched

11. `401 response clears authToken` — call setAuthToken('my-jwt'), mock 401, call get(), verify getAuthToken() is null after the error

**Keep existing tests that still apply:**
- `fetchApi injects auth token as Bearer header when authenticated` — update to use setAuthToken() instead of resetAuthState()/initAuth()
- `fetchApi does not override explicit Authorization header` — update to use setAuthToken()
- `onAuthStateChange unsubscribe prevents further callbacks` — update to use setAuthToken/setAuthState instead of initAuth
- `onAuthStateChange fires on state transitions` — update to use setAuthToken/setAuthState

## Files to Create

None.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **sse.ts full token exchange rewrite** — sse.ts still uses getAuthToken() in getSSEUrl() to pass token as query param. Task .23 (SSE Token Exchange) will replace this with the opaque token exchange pattern (GET /api/events/token). This task only removes the initAuth import.
- **agents.ts, observability.ts, usage.ts, logs.ts, sessions.ts** — these files import getAuthToken directly for raw fetch calls. Task .28 (Migrate direct getAuthToken consumers) handles migrating them to fetchApi. This task does not touch them.
- **Boot sequence conditional rendering** — main.tsx will render the same provider tree as today (minus initAuth). Task .21 (Boot Sequence Rewiring) adds the fetchAppConfig → conditional ExternalAuthProvider/NoAuthProvider wrapping.

## Dependencies

### No external packages needed
This is purely a removal/simplification task.

### No blocking task dependencies
This task's only dependency is the parent epic (laf73). It can be implemented immediately.

### What this task blocks
- **loomcli-laf73.16** (AuthContext) — depends on setAuthToken() and setAuthState() exports, and the 'auth-token-expired' CustomEvent
- **loomcli-laf73.28** (Migrate direct getAuthToken consumers) — depends on initAuth being removed (consumers switch to fetchApi)

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **SSE reconnection with 'failed' state**: sse.ts currently checks `getAuthState() === 'failed'` && `getAuthToken() === null` before attempting reconnection with re-auth via initAuth. After this change, the initAuth call is removed but the state check remains. When SSE encounters this state, it will simply skip the re-auth block and proceed to connect without a token. The full SSE auth handling is deferred to task .23.

2. **Race: 401 event dispatch vs. error throw**: The 401 handler dispatches the CustomEvent synchronously, then falls through to throw ApiError. Since dispatchEvent is synchronous, AuthContext's listener will be invoked before the throw. However, the listener only triggers an async session refresh — it doesn't synchronously provide a new token. The throwing request will still fail with 401. Subsequent requests (after the session refresh completes) will use the new token naturally. This is the intended behavior.

3. **Multiple concurrent 401s**: If 5 API calls all get 401 simultaneously, each will:
   - Clear authToken (idempotent after first)
   - Dispatch 'auth-token-expired' (5 events)
   - Throw ApiError(401)
   AuthContext's debounced refresh handler (.16 design) deduplicates these — only one getSession() call fires within the debounce window.

4. **AuthState type export compatibility**: Consumers using the string values 'disabled' or 'initializing' will get TypeScript compile errors. This is intentional — catches all callsites at build time. The only consumers are:
   - main.tsx (lines 69, 74) — modified in this task
   - sse.ts (line 122) — checks for 'failed', not 'disabled' or 'initializing', so no breakage
   - client.test.ts — rewritten in this task

5. **setAuthToken during fetchApi execution**: If AuthContext calls setAuthToken() while a fetchApi call is in flight, the in-flight request already has its headers set and won't be affected. The next request will pick up the new token. This is correct and expected.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (client.test.ts)
See "Files to Modify" section 5 for the complete test plan.

Key scenarios:
- setAuthToken lifecycle (set, clear, state transitions)
- setAuthState direct manipulation
- onAuthStateChange subscription/unsubscription
- fetchApi Bearer header injection with setAuthToken
- 401 handler dispatches CustomEvent and clears token
- 401 handler skips dispatch when token is null
- Explicit Authorization header preservation

### Build Verification
```bash
cd internal/webui/frontend
npx tsc --noEmit          # TypeScript type checking — catches any 'disabled'/'initializing' references
npm run build             # Full Vite production build
npm test                  # Run all tests
```

### Manual Verification
- Run `loom serve` — verify app loads without console errors about initAuth
- Verify API calls work in no-auth mode (no Authorization header sent)
- Check browser console for no 'initAuth' or '/api/auth/token' references
- Verify SSE connection still works (no initAuth call, falls through gracefully)
close_reason: Completed: removed initAuth, pendingAuthPromise, isTransientFailure, _retried param. Simplified AuthState to none|authenticated|failed. Added setAuthToken/setAuthState exports. Replaced 401 retry interceptor with CustomEvent dispatch. All 292 test files pass, quality gate green.

title: Go: Wire ExtAuth Middleware and ServerConfig
description:
Wire NewExtAuthMiddleware into the middleware chain at the same slot NewAuthMiddleware occupied (between SecurityHeaders and CORS). CRITICAL: NewExtAuthMiddleware MUST call isPublicRoute() (from auth_routes.go, extracted by .26) as its first check. Exempt routes: /api/fleet/*, /api/terminal/ws, /api/agents/*/terminal/ws, /api/internal/workers/*, GET /api/events, POST /api/sessions/notify, /health, /api/health, /api/client-errors, /api/csp-report, /api/config, all non-/api/ paths.

SECURITY — HTTPS enforcement: Refuse HTTP for --auth-url unless hostname is literally localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1. Non-loopback HTTP means MITM on JWKS = inject arbitrary public keys = forge JWTs. Add --auth-allow-insecure flag (with loud startup warning) as escape hatch for Docker internal networks that use HTTP between containers.

SECURITY — CSP update: When ExtAuthURL is configured, dynamically add the auth service origin to CSP connect-src. Do NOT use wildcards. Pass ExtAuthURL to SecurityConfig.

SECURITY — iss/aud REQUIRED: When --auth-url is set, issuer and audience are always validated. Default --auth-issuer to --auth-url value, default --auth-audience to "loom". These are defaults, NOT optional — the parser always checks iss and aud. Add startup health check: after JWKS cache initializes, log the first JWKS key IDs so operators can audit what keys are trusted. If possible, fetch a test token from the auth service at startup and verify iss/aud match — catch mismatches at startup, not at first user request.

SECURITY — Open mode warning: When --auth-url is NOT set AND --bind is non-loopback, refuse to start or display prominent warning.

SECURITY — CORS: Auto-add ExtAuthURL origin to Go CORS allowed origins when --auth-url is set.

ORDERING: This task MUST merge BEFORE .8 (Remove API Key Auth). Old NewAuthMiddleware remains until this is tested. In serve.go: --auth-url (env LOOM_AUTH_URL), --auth-issuer (env LOOM_AUTH_ISSUER), --auth-audience (env LOOM_AUTH_AUDIENCE), --auth-allow-insecure (no env default). Add to ServerConfig: ExtAuthURL, ExtAuthIssuer, ExtAuthAudience, ExtAuthAllowInsecure.
design:
## Summary

Wire the external JWT authentication middleware into the WebUI server's middleware chain and make it configurable via CLI flags, environment variables, and ServerConfig fields. When `ExtAuthURL` is set, the server derives the JWKS endpoint (`{ExtAuthURL}/api/auth/jwks`), initializes a JWKS key cache, constructs `NewExtAuthMiddleware`, and inserts it at the same position in the middleware chain that `NewAuthMiddleware` previously occupied. When `ExtAuthURL` is empty, the middleware is a passthrough (open mode). This task also wires CSP `connect-src` and CORS `AllowedOrigins` to dynamically include the auth service origin, and adds an open-mode warning when binding to non-loopback addresses without auth.

## Technical Approach

**Strategy**: Config + plumbing only. Add four new fields to `ServerConfig`, add four CLI flags to `serve.go`, extend `SecurityConfig` with an optional auth origin for CSP, auto-add the auth origin to CORS allowed origins, and wire the initialization/teardown of `JWKSCache` + `NewExtAuthMiddleware` into `StartServer()`. No new files created — all changes are in existing files.

**Key design decisions:**

1. **ExtAuthURL is the auth service base URL, NOT the JWKS endpoint URL**: `ExtAuthURL` is the base URL of the Better Auth service (e.g., `https://auth.loomcli.com`). The JWKS endpoint URL is derived by appending `/api/auth/jwks` (Better Auth's default JWKS path). This means `NewJWKSCache` receives `cfg.ExtAuthURL + "/api/auth/jwks"` as its endpoint parameter. This clarifies the semantic: `ExtAuthURL` identifies the auth service, and the JWKS path is an implementation detail of Better Auth.

2. **Middleware chain position**: `NewExtAuthMiddleware` replaces `NewAuthMiddleware` in the same slot. The chain order is: RequestLog → RateLimit → SecurityHeaders → **ExtAuth** → CORS → mux. This means CORS preflight OPTIONS pass through without auth, and security headers apply to all responses including 401s — same invariant as the old auth middleware.

3. **Passthrough when unconfigured**: When `ExtAuthURL` is empty (the zero value), no JWKS cache is created and the middleware returns a passthrough. This preserves backward compatibility — existing deployments that don't set `--auth-url` behave exactly as they do today (no auth).

4. **JWKS cache lifecycle**: Created in `StartServer()` with `NewJWKSCache(jwksURL, nil, config.Logger)` where `jwksURL = cfg.ExtAuthURL + "/api/auth/jwks"`. The nil HTTP client causes it to create a safe client internally (SSRF-protected via `safeDialContext`). `defer jwksCache.Stop()` ensures the background refresh goroutine is shut down on server exit.

5. **Startup health check uses initial fetch log**: The JWKS cache's `NewJWKSCache()` already performs an initial synchronous fetch and logs a warning on failure (per .5 design). The `GetKey` method is the only public method besides `Stop()` — there is no `GetAllKeyIDs()` method. Instead, the startup log message reports whether the initial fetch succeeded or failed: `slog.Info("external auth enabled", "jwks_url", jwksURL)` after construction, plus the JWKS cache's own internal logging on fetch success/failure. No additional key enumeration is needed.

6. **URL validation in serve.go**: The `--auth-url` flag value is validated before passing to `ServerConfig`: must parse as valid URL with scheme `http` or `https`. If `http` is used with a non-loopback hostname (not localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1), refuse to start with a fatal error. Loopback HTTP is allowed with a warning. `--auth-allow-insecure` overrides the refusal for Docker internal networks.

7. **CSP connect-src dynamic update**: When `ExtAuthURL` is configured, add the auth service origin to `SecurityConfig` so the CSP `connect-src` directive includes it. This allows the frontend's Better Auth SDK to make API calls (OAuth redirects, session checks) to the auth service. No wildcards. The origin is extracted from `ExtAuthURL` using `url.Parse` (scheme + host only).

8. **CORS auto-add**: When `ExtAuthURL` is configured, the auth service origin is automatically added to `corsConfig.AllowedOrigins` in `StartServer()`. CORS is also force-enabled if not already. This allows the frontend to make cross-origin requests to the auth service (OAuth flows, session management). The origin is extracted from `ExtAuthURL` using `url.Parse` (scheme + host only).

9. **Open mode warning**: When `ExtAuthURL` is NOT set AND the bind address is non-loopback (not `127.0.0.1`, not `::1`, not `localhost`), log a prominent warning: "WARNING: No authentication configured and server is exposed to network. Any client can access all API endpoints." This catches misconfiguration where a server is exposed without auth. It does NOT refuse to start (that would break existing local dev workflows where users bind to `0.0.0.0` for testing).

10. **Ordering: .13 MUST land BEFORE .8**: This task wires `NewExtAuthMiddleware` into the chain while the old `NewAuthMiddleware` still exists. The old auth middleware remains operational until .13 is tested and verified. Only then does .8 (Remove API Key Auth) remove `NewAuthMiddleware`, `AuthConfig`, `APIKey`, and `AuthEnabled`. This ordering prevents a window where no auth middleware exists. In the interim, when `ExtAuthURL` is set, the new middleware replaces the old one in the chain. When `ExtAuthURL` is empty, the old middleware continues to function.

## Conventions Established

- **`ExtAuthURL` is the auth service base URL**: All tasks that reference the JWKS endpoint should derive it as `{ExtAuthURL}/api/auth/jwks`. The `/api/auth/jwks` suffix is Better Auth's default path and is appended internally, not exposed as a config flag.
- **Auth origin extraction**: Use `url.Parse(ExtAuthURL)` then `u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host` to extract the origin for CSP and CORS. This is used in both `SecurityConfig.ExtAuthOrigin` and the CORS auto-add logic.
- **Issuer defaults to ExtAuthURL**: When `--auth-issuer` is not provided, it defaults to the `--auth-url` value. When `--auth-audience` is not provided, it defaults to `"loom"`.

## Files to Create

None. All changes are modifications to existing files.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/server_config.go`

Add four new fields to `ServerConfig`:

```go
ExtAuthURL            string // Auth service base URL (e.g., "https://auth.loomcli.com"); empty = open mode
ExtAuthIssuer         string // Expected JWT issuer (validated against "iss" claim; defaults to ExtAuthURL)
ExtAuthAudience       string // Expected JWT audience (validated against "aud" claim; defaults to "loom")
ExtAuthAllowInsecure  bool   // Allow HTTP for non-loopback --auth-url (escape hatch for Docker networks)
```

Place them after the existing `HSTSEnabled` field (grouping security-related config together). No changes to `DefaultConfig()` needed — zero values mean "disabled" which is correct.

### 2. `internal/webui/security.go`

**a) Add `ExtAuthOrigin` field to `SecurityConfig`**:

```go
type SecurityConfig struct {
    HSTSEnabled    bool
    ExtAuthOrigin  string // Auth service origin to add to CSP connect-src (e.g., "https://auth.loomcli.com")
}
```

**b) Update CSP `connect-src` construction** in `NewSecurityHeadersMiddleware`:

Replace the hardcoded CSP string with dynamic construction when `cfg.ExtAuthOrigin` is set:

```go
connectSrc := "'self'"
if cfg.ExtAuthOrigin != "" {
    connectSrc += " " + cfg.ExtAuthOrigin
}
csp := fmt.Sprintf(
    "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-E907z9SPF4o7blRe1MXfQVC2tBrJopXOXrMYZvksy/o='; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src %s; font-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; report-uri /api/csp-report",
    connectSrc,
)
h.Set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)
```

This keeps the same CSP when `ExtAuthOrigin` is empty (backward compatible) and dynamically adds the auth service origin when configured. No wildcards — the origin is a specific `scheme://host` value.

### 3. `internal/webui/server.go`

In `StartServer()`, three changes:

**a) CORS auto-add** (after the existing CORS config block, around line 62):

```go
// When external auth is configured, ensure CORS includes the auth service origin
// so the frontend's Better Auth SDK can make cross-origin requests (OAuth, session mgmt).
if config.ExtAuthURL != "" {
    authOrigin := extractOrigin(config.ExtAuthURL)
    if authOrigin != "" {
        if !corsConfig.Enabled {
            corsConfig.Enabled = true
        }
        corsConfig.AllowedOrigins = append(corsConfig.AllowedOrigins, authOrigin)
    }
}
```

Where `extractOrigin` is a small helper (add at bottom of server.go or inline):

```go
// extractOrigin returns the scheme://host portion of a URL, suitable for
// CORS and CSP origin matching.
func extractOrigin(rawURL string) string {
    u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
    if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
        return ""
    }
    return u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host
}
```

Add `"net/url"` to imports if not already present.

**b) Open mode warning** (after the existing `if config.HSTSEnabled` log block, around line 76):

```go
// Warn if no auth and exposed to network
if config.ExtAuthURL == "" && config.BindAddress != "127.0.0.1" && config.BindAddress != "::1" {
    slog.Warn("no authentication configured and server is exposed to network — any client can access all API endpoints",
        "bind_address", config.BindAddress)
}
```

**c) JWKS cache + ExtAuth middleware initialization** (replace the existing API key auth block at lines 346-367):

When `ExtAuthURL` is set, initialize JWKS cache and ExtAuth middleware. When empty, use passthrough. In the interim (before .8 removes old auth), when `ExtAuthURL` is set the old auth middleware is effectively replaced. When `ExtAuthURL` is empty, the old auth middleware continues to function.

```go
// Initialize external auth (JWKS cache + middleware)
var extAuthMiddleware func(http.Handler) http.Handler
if config.ExtAuthURL != "" {
```

## Dependencies

**External packages**: None new. All needed packages are already in go.mod:
- `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` (used by ext_auth.go, created by .7)
- `golang.org/x/net/http2` and `h2c` (existing)

**Blocks**:
- loomcli-laf73.8 (Remove API Key Auth) — depends on this task being tested first
- loomcli-laf73.18 (GET /api/config) — depends on `isPublicRoute` update from this task
- loomcli-laf73.20 (SSE Token Exchange) — depends on auth middleware being wired

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **JWKS endpoint unreachable at startup**: `NewJWKSCache` performs initial fetch but logs a warning on failure (doesn't block startup). First request needing auth will get 401 until keys are fetched. The startup log reports the JWKS URL so operators can diagnose connectivity issues.

2. **ExtAuthURL set but Issuer/Audience empty**: Defaults are applied in serve.go before constructing ServerConfig. Issuer defaults to ExtAuthURL, Audience defaults to "loom". The parser always checks iss and aud against these defaults. This prevents misconfiguration where tokens from one deployment are accepted by another.

3. **HTTPS enforcement**: HTTP is refused for `--auth-url` unless the hostname is literally `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1`. Non-loopback HTTP means MITM on JWKS = inject arbitrary public keys = forge JWTs. `--auth-allow-insecure` flag (with loud startup warning) is the escape hatch for Docker internal networks.

4. **JWKS cache lifecycle**: `defer jwksCache.Stop()` in `StartServer()` ensures the background refresh goroutine is cleaned up on shutdown. This is critical to avoid goroutine leaks.

5. **Middleware ordering**: ExtAuth MUST be between SecurityHeaders (outer) and CORS (inner). This ensures: (a) security headers are set on 401 responses, (b) CORS preflight OPTIONS bypass auth. The middleware chain comment documents this invariant.

6. **isPublicRoute for /api/config**: The config endpoint MUST be public (exempt from auth) because the frontend needs to discover the auth mode before it can obtain a JWT. Without this exemption, external auth creates a chicken-and-egg problem.

7. **CSP connect-src injection safety**: The auth origin is extracted via `url.Parse` (scheme + host only) — no path, query, or fragment. This prevents injection of arbitrary CSP directives via a malicious `--auth-url` value. The origin is appended to `connect-src`, not interpolated into other directives.

8. **CORS auto-add idempotency**: If the user already specified the auth origin in `--cors`, it will appear twice in AllowedOrigins. The `allowedMap` in `NewCORSMiddleware` deduplicates via map keys, so this is harmless.

9. **Backward compatibility**: When `ExtAuthURL` is empty (the zero value), the middleware is a no-op passthrough, CORS is unchanged, CSP is unchanged, and the old auth middleware continues to function. Existing deployments that don't set `--auth-url` are completely unaffected.

10. **Open mode warning**: When `ExtAuthURL` is empty AND bind is non-loopback, a warning is logged but the server still starts. This is intentional — refusing to start would break existing workflows. The warning alerts operators to the risk.

11. **Flag/env var naming**: `--auth-url` / `LOOM_AUTH_URL` follows the existing pattern of `--redis-addr` / `LOOM_REDIS_ADDR`. Consistent naming helps users discover configuration.

12. **Coexistence with old auth**: When `ExtAuthURL` is set, `activeAuthMiddleware` uses the new ExtAuth middleware. When empty, it uses the old `NewAuthMiddleware`. Both never run simultaneously in the chain. After .8 removes old auth, the else branch becomes a simple passthrough.

## Testing Strategy

### Automated Tests

Run after implementation:
```bash
go test ./internal/webui/... -count=1
go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1
go build ./cmd/loom/
```

### Key Scenarios to Cover

1. **Server starts with ExtAuthURL set**: `TestStartServer_ExtAuthEnabled` — provide a mock JWKS endpoint URL, verify server initializes JWKS cache, verify authenticated requests with valid JWT reach handlers, verify unauthenticated requests to protected routes return 401.

2. **Server starts without ExtAuthURL (open mode)**: `TestStartServer_ExtAuthDisabled` — `ExtAuthURL` is empty, verify all requests pass through without ext-auth (old auth behavior applies per `AuthEnabled` flag).

3. **CLI flag parsing**: Verify `--auth-url`, `--auth-issuer`, `--auth-audience`, `--auth-allow-insecure` are registered and map to the correct `ServerConfig` fields. Verify env var defaults (`LOOM_AUTH_URL`, `LOOM_AUTH_ISSUER`, `LOOM_AUTH_AUDIENCE`).

4. **URL validation**: Verify `--auth-url ftp://bad` and `--auth-url not-a-url` are rejected. Verify `--auth-url http://example.com` is refused with fatal error (non-loopback HTTP). Verify `--auth-url http://example.com --auth-allow-insecure` is accepted with loud warning. Verify `--auth-url https://example.com` is accepted without warning. Verify `--auth-url http://localhost:3000` is accepted with warning (loopback HTTP OK).

5. **CSP connect-src**: `TestSecurityHeaders_ExtAuthOriginInCSP` — verify CSP includes auth origin. `TestSecurityHeaders_NoExtAuth_DefaultCSP` — verify default CSP unchanged when no auth.

6. **isPublicRoute /api/config**: Verify `isPublicRoute("GET", "/api/config")` returns `true`. Verify workspace-scoped variant also works: `isPublicRoute("GET", "/api/workspaces/ws1/config")`.

7. **Middleware chain order**: Verify that 401 responses from ExtAuth include security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.). This confirms the middleware ordering is correct.

8. **JWKS URL derivation**: Verify that the JWKS cache receives `{ExtAuthURL}/api/auth/jwks` as its endpoint, not the raw `ExtAuthURL`.

9. **CORS auto-add**: Verify that when `ExtAuthURL` is set, the auth origin appears in the CORS allowed origins list.

10. **Open mode warning**: Verify that when `ExtAuthURL` is empty and bind is `0.0.0.0`, a warning is logged.

### Manual Verification

1. `loom serve --help` should show `--auth-url`, `--auth-issuer`, `--auth-audience`, `--auth-allow-insecure` flags.
2. `loom serve` (no auth flags) should start without auth-related log messages (except open-mode warning if bound to non-loopback).
3. `loom serve --auth-url https://auth.example.com` should log "external auth enabled" with JWKS URL `https://auth.example.com/api/auth/jwks`.
4. With ext auth enabled: `curl localhost:8080/api/issues` → 401. `curl localhost:8080/health` → 200. `curl localhost:8080/api/config` → 200.
5. `loom serve --auth-url ftp://bad` → fatal error message about invalid URL.
6. `loom serve --auth-url http://remote.example.com` → fatal error about non-loopback HTTP.
7. `loom serve --auth-url http://remote.example.com --auth-allow-insecure` → warning but starts.
8. Check CSP header when auth is configured: `curl -I localhost:8080/` → CSP connect-src should include auth origin.
